Its agents handle revenue cycle management (eligibility and insurance verification, prior authorization, claim status checking, denials management, and patient refunds), patient access, and other repetitive tasks by working inside a customer's existing EHR, practice-management, and payer systems either through APIs or the same screens staff use. Clicks integrates with major health IT platforms including Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, ModMed, NextGen Healthcare, and MEDITECH, and states it is SOC 2 Type II audited and HIPAA compliant with end-to-end encryption for PHI. Founded in 2025, headquartered in Switzerland, and backed by Y Combinator (F2025).

providers.name: DocStation
providers.description: DocStation is a unified pharmacy care and medical billing platform that helps community and clinical pharmacies move beyond prescription dispensing to bill insurance for the clinical services they already provide — vaccines, MTM, point-of-care testing, consultations, and DME. The platform consolidates 360-degree patient records, automated medical claims generation and resubmission, smart scheduling with public booking links, connected SMS and organization-to-organization messaging, workflow automation, and live revenue analytics into a single system. It integrates with pharmacy management systems (PioneerRx, Liberty, DRX), 1,000+ health plans, clearinghouses, and state immunization registries. DocStation is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II audited. Backed by Techstars; added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from its public surface. No public developer API is documented at this time.

providers.name: KRY | LIVI
providers.description: KRY International AB is Europe's largest digital-first healthcare provider, founded in Stockholm in 2015 by Johannes Schildt. It delivers primary and specialist care through a mobile and web app — video and chat consultations with doctors, nurses, psychologists and physiotherapists — combined with a network of physical clinics. The company trades as KRY in Sweden, Norway and Germany and as Livi in the United Kingdom and France, and reports more than 14 million patient appointments, 4,000+ healthcare professionals and 60+ clinics. Alongside consumer care it sells digital clinical capacity to public payers (including the NHS and Swedish regions), employers, insurers and Employee Assistance Programmes. KRY publishes no public developer portal, API reference or SDKs; its consumer and partner surfaces are app- and contract-based, and patient authentication in Sweden runs on BankID.

providers.name: WellSky
providers.description: WellSky provides care coordination and home health software with REST APIs for managing patient referrals, authorizations, visit scheduling, clinical documentation, and billing workflows across home health, hospice, palliative care, personal care, and specialty pharmacy settings.

providers.name: Chewy
providers.description: Chewy, Inc. is a Fortune 500 American online retailer of pet food, pet products, prescription medications, and veterinary services headquartered in Plantation, Florida. Chewy is one of the largest e-commerce pet retailers in the United States and supports a customer-focused operating model centered on subscription Autoship orders, Chewy Pharmacy prescription fulfillment, Connect with a Vet telehealth, and Chewy Health insurance. Chewy provides vendor and supplier integration primarily through the Dsco supplier integration platform rather than a public consumer-facing developer API. The Dsco-based integration supports core EDI transactions for purchase orders, inventory updates, shipment confirmations, and invoices, enabling brands and third-party logistics providers to connect with Chewy's e-commerce marketplace.

providers.name: Kyo
providers.description: Kyo (kyocare.com) is a US provider of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) therapy for autistic children and young adults, delivering in-home, in-school and center-based care across 20+ locations with in-network coverage from major insurers. Kyo runs a client-facing digital surface — the Kyo Care portal and mobile app — for scheduling, session notes, progress tracking and family communication, backed by the internal "Attain" platform API (api.attain.kyocare.com) that publishes live OpenID Connect and RFC 8414 discovery documents over AWS Cognito, plus a private Workato-managed partner gateway at api.kyocare.com. Kyo publishes no public developer program, documentation or SDKs; its API surface is private to its own applications and payer integrations.

providers.name: Unite Us
providers.description: Unite Us is the software and data infrastructure company for coordinating whole-person care across healthcare, government, and community-based organizations. Its platform screens people for social determinants of health, sends closed-loop referrals to community services, and tracks outcomes, with EHR and case-management integrations (Epic, Oracle Health, Meditech, Salesforce) delivered through FHIR APIs, SMART on FHIR apps, and other HL7 protocols aligned with Gravity Project standards. The platform is HIPAA-compliant and HITRUST, SOC 2 Type 2, and NIST CSF certified. API and integration documentation is gated to licensed network partners.

providers.name: Kalderos
providers.description: Kalderos is a Chicago-based healthcare technology company, founded in 2016, that built what it calls the first Drug Discount Management platform. It helps pharmaceutical manufacturers, covered entities (safety-net healthcare providers), and state Medicaid programs manage compliance across U.S. drug discount programs — most notably 340B — using data, AI, and machine learning to identify noncompliant or duplicate discounts, streamline good-faith-inquiry and dispute resolution, and move rebates transparently between stakeholders. Marquee products include 340B Pay, the Truzo rebate-payment platform, Discount Hub for covered entities, and MDRP and Commercial Discount Monitoring for manufacturers. Kalderos was acquired by Model N in 2024 to expand Model N's revenue-management and 340B capabilities for life sciences. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Kalderos operates a customer-facing application (app.kalderos.com) and previously published developer API documentation that is no longer resolvable post-acquisition.

providers.name: OpenPrescribing
providers.description: OpenPrescribing.net is an open-data service built and operated by the Bennett Institute for Applied Data Science at the University of Oxford. It turns the English Prescribing Dataset published monthly by the NHS Business Services Authority into public dashboards, prescribing-safety measures, and a free RESTful API covering primary-care GP prescribing across England. The API exposes spending, quantity and item counts by BNF code and by NHS organisation (practice, PCN, Sub-ICB Location, ICB, Regional Team), standardised prescribing measures, drug-tariff and price-per-unit data, and organisation reference/boundary lookups, all returned as JSON, CSV or GeoJSON. Home market is the United Kingdom (England prescribing data). It is an independent academic analytics platform layered on NHS open data, not an NHS FHIR clinical system; there is no OAuth, no SMART-on-FHIR, and currently no registration or API key is required.

providers.name: Superpower
providers.description: Superpower is a consumer preventive-health and longevity membership that provides an annual comprehensive blood draw across 100+ biomarkers, AI-driven result interpretation, biological age scoring, personalized action plans, and a care team, delivered through web and mobile apps. As of the catalog date Superpower does not publish a public or partner developer API; this catalog documents the product surface honestly rather than fabricating endpoints.

providers.name: Dentsply Sirona
providers.description: Dentsply Sirona is the world's largest manufacturer of professional dental products and technologies, providing comprehensive solutions for dentists, dental laboratories, and dental specialists worldwide. The company exposes developer integrations through DS Core, an open cloud platform, and through the Dentsply Sirona Imaging modality API for intraoral imaging hardware.

providers.name: Insight Health
providers.description: Insight Health builds AI clinical agents that handle the patient-facing workflows clinical staff spend the most time on: phone answering, fax processing, ambient note-taking, intake, follow-up, referral management, and triage. Built by practicing physicians, the platform is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, and integrates with the major outpatient EHRs via FHIR R4 and HL7v2. Its voice agent Lumi handled the first known autonomous clinical AI conversation with a patient in October 2023, and the company has since handled more than 4 million patient conversations across 60+ medical specialties. Products include Aura AI Scribe, the Aura Anywhere embedded scribe SDK for EHR vendors, AI FrontDesk, AI Fax Agent, Pre-Visit Intake, Follow-up, Referral Management, and Phone Triage agents.

providers.name: Modern Health
providers.description: Modern Health is a global mental health benefits platform that employers offer to their workforce, positioning itself as "the global standard in mental health" with evidence-based, equitable care delivered worldwide. Its Adaptive Care Model spans self-guided digital tools, 1:1 coaching, therapy and counseling, group support Circles, and crisis care, matched to members through a Stepped Care methodology. The platform serves employers, benefits consultants, health plans, and providers, delivering care in 80+ languages across a proprietary provider network spanning 200+ countries and territories. Modern Health does not publish a public developer API; its surfaces are member and admin web/mobile applications, a status page, and a security/trust program. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and enriched with the company's real operational, security, and legal surface.

providers.name: Radical Health
providers.description: Radical Health is a Khosla Ventures-backed healthcare AI company that produces personalized, expert-reviewed cancer treatment reports for patients in the United States. Its platform ingests a patient's medical records and synthesizes oncology research, clinical trials, and prior patient outcomes into a tailored report within days, drawing on 5.3 million research papers, 11.8 million patient journeys, 20,000 treatment options, and 48,800+ active US clinical trials. The service pairs an always-on AI nurse navigator ("Alice") with human oncology oversight from institutions including UCLA, Johns Hopkins, Stanford, and Kaiser Permanente, and connects to 70,000+ US healthcare institutions (Epic, Kaiser, Ascension, HCA, Medicare) for records access. Reports are informational and educational only, not medical advice. Radical Health is HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II certified and operates as a consumer subscription product ($110/month with a 7-day free trial); it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Counsel Health
providers.description: Counsel Health is a telemedicine company multiplying the world's healthcare capacity by pairing an AI medical assistant with board-certified physicians delivered through chat. Individuals get free AI medical guidance and can connect with a licensed doctor for a flat $29 per consultation, seven days a week, for urgent care, primary care support, medication refills, lab testing, and health-record management. Counsel also ships an embedded product — a WebView / iFrame surface plus a server-side Counsel API — that partners integrate into their own applications, documented at docs.counselhealth.com with example apps published on GitHub. Backed by GV (Google Ventures).

providers.name: OSCAR EMR
providers.description: OSCAR EMR is an open-source electronic medical record (EMR) system created by Dr. David Chan and McMaster University's Department of Family Medicine, and one of Canada's most widely deployed primary-care EMRs. The core software is distributed under the GPL v2+ license (mirrored on GitHub as scoophealth/oscar and on Bitbucket), while the commercially supported OSCAR Pro distribution is delivered by the WELL EMR Group (a WELL Health company) to more than 2,000 clinics and 10,000 providers across Canada. OSCAR exposes a documented REST web-services API under the /ws/services path (scheduling, demographics, billing, prescriptions, documents, labs, ticklers, eForms and providers), secured with 3-legged OAuth 1.0a via /ws/oauth. Clinical data flows historically use HL7 v2 messaging, and OSCAR ships an internal HL7 FHIR integration used for Ontario public-health and immunization reporting (BORN, DHIR). Third-party integrations for OSCAR Pro are partner-gated through the apps.health marketplace. As self-hosted software there is no single public API host or hosted FHIR CapabilityStatement; the API surface is documented on the OSCAR EMR developer wiki and realized per clinic deployment.

providers.name: Anthem
providers.description: Anthem, Inc. (now operating as Elevance Health) is one of the largest health benefits companies in the United States, serving members through affiliated Blue Cross and Blue Shield health plans across multiple states including California, New York, Virginia, Georgia, and others. Anthem provides health insurance, pharmacy benefits, and behavioral health services to over 40 million members. Under CMS interoperability rules (CMS-9115-F), Anthem offers FHIR- based Patient Access and Provider Directory APIs.

providers.name: Medigate
providers.description: Medigate was a healthcare IoT / connected-medical-device cybersecurity company (headquartered in Brooklyn, NY, backed by Partech and others) that built the first security platform dedicated to healthcare IoT — device discovery, risk assessment, and clinically-aware network segmentation for hospitals. Claroty completed its acquisition of Medigate on 2022-01-10 and folded the product into "Claroty xDome for Healthcare"; the standalone brand is retired and medigate.io now redirects to claroty.com. A residual customer-facing REST API remains live at api.medigate.io (with a password-gated interactive reference at api.medigate.io/docs) that integrations use to pull device inventory, device groups, and device risk scores.

providers.name: Stryker
providers.description: Stryker Corporation is a Fortune 500 medical technologies company offering products in orthopedics, medical and surgical equipment, and neurotechnology and spine. Stryker provides Connected OR integration platforms and Smart Equipment Management (SEM) systems for healthcare facilities. The company does not currently offer a publicly documented developer API. Stryker's digital health products include the Mako robotic arm for orthopedic surgery, iSuite integrated OR technology, and asset tracking systems. Integration with hospital EHR and OR management systems is done through vendor partnerships rather than public APIs.

providers.name: Vivoo
providers.description: Vivoo is a wellness technology company offering science-backed, at-home urine test strips paired with a mobile app that turns results into personalized nutrition and lifestyle recommendations. Its lineup includes the 8-parameter Vivoo Wellness Test, an at-home UTI test, fertility/ovulation and vaginal pH tests, and a connected Smart Toilet. The direct-to-consumer store runs on Shopify and exposes a native agent-commerce surface: a published llms.txt/agents.md, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, and a hosted UCP shopping MCP server for agent-driven catalog search, cart, and buyer-approved checkout. Backed by 500 Global and Techstars.

providers.name: Fasten Health
providers.description: Fasten Health is a healthcare data interoperability company offering a unified medical record platform that gives patients and developers access to clinical data across the U.S. healthcare system. Fasten began as an open-source project — Fasten OnPrem, a self-hosted personal/family electronic medical record manager that ingests FHIR Bundles and is distributed under GPL-3.0 with 2.7k+ GitHub stars. The team then productized the connectivity layer as Fasten Connect, a commercial REST + FHIR API and Stitch client SDK suite that lets developers retrieve clinical records from 50,000+ healthcare systems and 60,000+ organizations including Epic, Cerner, MyChart, Kaiser Permanente, HCA, Ascension, Humana, and Medicare. Founded by engineers who lived through the fragmentation of health data firsthand and based in New York City, Fasten ships GPL/MIT/Apache 2.0 open source repos alongside the hosted Fasten Connect platform.

providers.name: CareFusion (BD)
providers.description: CareFusion is a medical technology brand, acquired by BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) in 2015, best known for the Alaris infusion system and the Pyxis automated dispensing product line. CareFusion does not expose a public developer API; instead, its devices and dispensing systems interoperate with hospital EMRs and pharmacy systems over HL7 v2 messaging, smart-pump interoperability middleware, and vendor-managed integration services. The Alaris Infusion Interoperability program wirelessly transmits orders from EMRs (such as Epic and Cerner) into Alaris large-volume and syringe modules and returns infusion status back to the EMR in near real time, using the Alaris Guardrails drug library as a safety layer.

providers.name: Klarify
providers.description: Klarify is a San Francisco and Canada based mental-health technology company building an AI assistant, "Klara", for licensed therapists. The product handles the administrative and operational work around therapy rather than the therapy itself: an AI scribe that turns recorded sessions into structured clinical notes across 20+ note formats, treatment-plan generation, clinical letters and assessment reports, insurance claim filing and form completion, session preparation, between-session client resources and worksheets, supervision prep, and visual session mindmaps, with support for many languages. Klarify also operates a public directory of licensed therapists and clinics across Canada and the US, where profiles, FAQs, and long-form articles are authored and verified by the clinicians themselves. The company states HIPAA, PIPEDA, PHIPA, and UK GDPR compliance, stores permanent records in Canada, deletes session audio after 14 days, and does not train models on customer session data. Founded in 2024 by Moody Abdul (CEO, previously co-founder of Circleback.ai) and Alexander Bergholm (CTO, formerly LLM infrastructure at Workday), Klarify is part of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch. Klarify publishes no public developer API: its llms.txt explicitly marks paths under /api/ as internal infrastructure.

providers.name: Mio
providers.description: Mio is a collaboration interoperability platform that connects the leading enterprise messaging tools so teams on different platforms can work together without switching apps. Positioned as Google's official interoperability partner, Mio provides API-based middleware that relays messages, files, and directory information between Google Chat, Microsoft Teams, Slack, and Zoom Team Chat. Its products include Chat Sync (cross-platform messaging), External Chat Sync (partner/federated collaboration), Directory Sync (bidirectional user directory synchronization), and File Sync (shared Google Drive and SharePoint links). Mio runs as native middleware built directly with the platform vendors, never persistently stores user messages or files, encrypts data in transit with TLS 1.2+ and at rest with AES-256, and holds SOC 2 Type II certification with GDPR and CCPA controls. Mio is sold as an enterprise offering rather than a self-serve public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and support surface.

providers.name: TrueCoach
providers.description: TrueCoach is a personal-training and remote-coaching platform for strength coaches, personal trainers, and physical therapists to deliver workouts online and train clients remotely. Started as Fitbot out of Techstars Boulder and now an Xplor Technologies brand, it offers a web app plus iOS and Android client apps with program and workout builders, a video exercise library, nutrition tracking, wearables data, Stripe-powered payments, a MyFitnessPal integration, and a Zapier connector — but publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Snap-on
providers.description: Snap-on Incorporated is a global manufacturer and marketer of tools, equipment, diagnostics, repair information, and systems solutions for professional users in vehicle repair, industrial, and other industries. The company provides diagnostic tools, electronic parts catalogs (EPC), repair information systems (ShopKey Pro, SureTrack), and shop management software. Snap-on integrates with dealer management systems (DMS) through its EPC integration program and strategic technology partnerships.

providers.name: WebPT
providers.description: WebPT is a rehabilitation-therapy software company providing a cloud practice-management platform for physical, occupational, and speech therapy and behavioral-health clinics. Its integrated suite spans clinical documentation and EMR, billing and revenue-cycle management, front-office scheduling and digital patient intake, benefits verification, home exercise programs, patient engagement and outcomes tracking, marketing, and practice analytics. WebPT connects to 60+ EHR and healthcare systems (Epic, athenahealth, Veradigm, McKesson, Meditech, Oracle Cloud, ModMed and others) through an integrations program built on HL7 interfaces (ADT, BAR, DFT, MDM/ORU). WebPT does not publish a public REST API, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition; integration is arranged through its partner and integrations program. WebPT is a Battery Ventures portfolio company.

providers.name: Alife
providers.description: Alife Health is an AI-powered fertility technology company building clinical decision-support tools for IVF clinics and fertility patients. Its Alife Assist platform integrates directly with clinic EMR systems and layers machine-learning models across the IVF cycle - Embryo Predict for AI-assisted embryo assessment and transfer decisions, Schedule Predict for optimizing egg-retrieval scheduling, and Success Predictor for patient success-likelihood modeling - alongside a patient-facing Alife App. Backed by Union Square Ventures. Alife does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its public web, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: CaptureProof
providers.description: CaptureProof is a HIPAA-compliant visual health record and telemedicine platform for secure photo and video communication between patients and clinicians. Its "Smart Medical Camera" iOS and Android apps let providers and patients capture consistent, medical-quality images and video, automatically organize and compare them chronologically, and layer AI-driven visual biometrics and clinical insight on top for remote patient monitoring, asynchronous ("visual voicemail") care, and post-op and chronic-condition follow-up. CaptureProof supports EHR/EMR integration and SSO handled by its technical team, and bills through remote-monitoring CPT codes. It is HIPAA, GDPR, and Swiss FADP aligned with AES-256 encryption. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Hammerhead
providers.description: Hammerhead is a cycling technology company (now part of SRAM) best known for the Karoo GPS cycling computer, a premium Android-based device for recording and displaying ride data, routes, structured workouts, and Flight Attendant performance. Its ecosystem includes the web Dashboard (dashboard.hammerhead.io) and a Companion mobile app that bridge ride data between rider, device, and third parties. Hammerhead runs one of the more open developer platforms in the category: a public API that lets connected third parties sync routes and workouts, and the karoo-ext Android/Kotlin Extensions SDK (io.hammerhead:karoo-ext, Apache-2.0) that lets developers build on-device extensions for Karoo and Karoo 2.

providers.name: kaiahealth
providers.description: Kaia Health is a digital therapeutics company founded in 2016 (New York and Munich) that delivers evidence-based, digital-first care for musculoskeletal (MSK) pain and respiratory conditions. Its smartphone apps use AI and computer vision (motion tracking) plus in-house physical-therapy doctors to guide members through clinically validated exercise and behavioral programs without appointments or wearable devices. Products include Kaia MSK (joint and muscle care) and Kaia Breathe (respiratory / COPD). The company sells to employers and health plans, claims 2,500+ enterprise clients and 3x ROI, and is HIPAA, GDPR, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 13485, and CE-certified. Kaia Health was acquired by Sword Health in January 2026. It is backed by Balderton Capital. Kaia Health publishes no public API; this profile captures its identity, security, and compliance posture.

providers.name: La Fraise Pro
providers.description: La Fraise (LA FRAISE PRO SAS) is a French SaaS platform that digitizes the administrative patient journey for dental practices and dental centers: interactive treatment quotes (devis), patient-education video, informed consent, mutual-insurer coverage requests, and compliant electronic signature, all handled remotely. The product integrates natively with the French dental practice-management market — LOGOSw, Julie, Veasy, CS Trophy, Visiodent, Ardion, WeClever, Desmos, Galaxie and Effigie — with real-time bidirectional sync for LOGOSw, Veasy and Desmos. More than 3,500 dentists are equipped. Patient data is hosted on HDS-certified AWS infrastructure in the European Union, in line with article L.1111-8 of the French Code de la sante publique, and electronic signature follows Agence du Numerique en Sante (ANS) norms. La Fraise publishes no public developer API; practice-management integrations are provisioned by its own technical team.

providers.name: Magical
providers.description: Magical is an AI-agent platform that automates repetitive administrative and operational workflows without requiring API integrations, instead driving the same web applications and databases a human worker would use. Originally known for its cross-application autofill and text-automation product, Magical has focused on healthcare operations, deploying specialized AI agents for patient access, revenue cycle management, prior authorizations, referrals, benefits verification, records requests, revenue integrity, and payment posting across EHR and payer systems such as Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, ModMed, Availity, and major insurers. Agents can be deployed individually or combined into autonomous suites, with the company reporting high task accuracy and multi-week deployment timelines. Magical is backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Greylock, and SV Angel. Notably, Magical operates through user-interface automation ("no APIs or integrations are required") rather than by exposing a public developer API.

providers.name: Apero
providers.description: Apero Health is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed healthcare technology company that provides an integrated practice-management and revenue-cycle-management (RCM) platform for medical practices. Its cloud software unifies scheduling, clinical visit notes, insurance eligibility verification and claims billing, patient billing and payments, e-prescriptions, and financial reporting, and claims to reduce billing time by up to 80% while helping practices scale operations. Apero exposes a fully-featured REST API, webhooks, and CSV import that connect healthcare and finance workflows, and integrates with payers (Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield) and platforms including Stripe, QuickBooks Online, Google, and Snowflake.

providers.name: Beacon Health
providers.description: Beacon Health (YC W26) is a San Francisco company building "AI employees" for primary care — autonomous agents that operate directly inside electronic health record systems the same way a human staff member does. Rather than integrating through an EHR vendor API, Beacon records a practice's existing workflow in the EHR (navigation, clicks, data entry) and converts that recording into a reusable, deployable agent that runs at scale across the whole patient panel. The agents automate value-based-care back-office work: preventative and quality gap closure, pre-charting, prior authorizations, referrals, transition-of-care management, and HCC risk-adjustment coding. Beacon advertises coverage of AthenaHealth, Epic, Cerner, eClinicalWorks, MEDITECH, NextGen, Veradigm Allscripts and MEDENT, plus payer portals and other web applications. Founded in 2025 by Mark Pothen (CEO) and Obinna Akahara (CTO), the company operates as a HIPAA Business Associate under a BAA with each covered entity. As of this profile Beacon Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition — the product is delivered as a managed agent workforce, not as a self-serve API.

providers.name: Ecton
providers.description: Ecton, Inc. is an AI-powered patient payments platform focused on reducing the financial stress and financial toxicity that surround healthcare costs. Its flagship product, Toni, is an AI financial counselor that gives patients personalized guidance on medical bills, insurance, and payment options, paired with a Health Savings and Spending Wallet for managing and paying healthcare expenses. Ecton helps healthcare providers strengthen patient relationships, improve treatment adherence, and increase revenue collection. The company is HIPAA-aligned and backed by General Catalyst. Ecton does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and public security posture.

providers.name: Fortuna Health
providers.description: Fortuna Health is a consumer-first Medicaid navigation platform that helps patients and members move through the Medicaid enrollment, recertification, appeals, and coverage-management processes end to end. Founded in 2023 and based in New York City, Fortuna consolidates the fragmented rules of the 50+ state and territory Medicaid programs — each with its own eligibility rules, documentation standards, and renewal timelines — into a single digital interface. The platform lets consumers connect accounts that auto-populate their filings, provides a virtual mailbox for state and health-plan communications, and sends text notifications for urgent, time-sensitive actions. Fortuna partners with health systems and managed care plans as middleware for the roughly $800B Medicaid ecosystem, and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Y Combinator.

providers.name: HumanFirst
providers.description: HumanFirst is a digital health measurement company whose Atlas platform helps clinical research and life-sciences teams evaluate, select, and operationalize sensor-based digital health technologies — wearables, connected devices, and digital biomarkers — for clinical trials and real-world evidence. Atlas curates a knowledge network of digital measures, connected devices, and the published evidence behind them so sponsors and CROs can choose fit-for-purpose measures. HumanFirst is now part of ICON plc and integrated into ICON's Digital Health Technologies (DHT) capabilities. The Atlas platform is delivered as an authenticated web application at app.gohumanfirst.com; the company does not currently publish a public developer API. This profile captures the company's public identity, security, and compliance posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: IDOVEN
providers.description: Idoven builds artificial-intelligence solutions for cardiovascular care. Its flagship platform, Willem, is a CE-marked Class IIa medical device that analyzes electrocardiograms (ECGs) to detect, diagnose, and monitor cardiac disease, identifying 22 cardiac patterns and 4 intervals across ambulatory devices, diagnostic ECGs, and insertable cardiac monitors. Idoven serves MedTech companies, Life Sciences (cardiotoxicity monitoring and disease-risk scoring for pharma trials), and preventative remote-screening programs. The Willem API supports bi-directional data exchange in EDF, HL7, DICOM, JSON, XML, and PDF. The company is headquartered in Spain, holds an extensive ISO and IEC certification program, and is backed by Insight Partners and Northzone. Sector: healthcare / cardiology AI.

providers.name: Koala Health
providers.description: Koala Health is a digital pet pharmacy headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts that dispenses prescription medications, vitamins, supplements and veterinary diets for dogs and cats direct to pet parents, with an emphasis on chronic-condition medication management. Orders are packaged into date- and time-sorted pouches, refilled automatically, and prescriptions are fetched and verified directly with the pet parent's veterinarian. Koala also runs KoalaVet, a clinic-facing platform that integrates with veterinary PIMS (practice information management systems) to sync client and patient records two-way, let clinic teams review, approve and submit prescriptions in a few clicks, and operate a branded managed online pharmacy for the practice. The company is a licensed non-resident pharmacy across US states, is LegitScript certified and .pharmacy (NABP) verified. Koala Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal or API documentation as of this profile; api.koala.health resolves to an internal Rails/Heroku administrative application behind sign-in.

providers.name: MedicalDirector
providers.description: MedicalDirector is an Australian clinical and practice-management software provider, owned by Telstra Health, that has served general practices, specialists, and day hospitals across Australia for more than 25 years. Its product family includes Helix (a cloud-based combined clinical and practice-management system), Clinical and Pracsoft (on-premise clinical and practice-management software), Bluechip (specialist practice management), and Day Surgery. Alongside Best Practice, MedicalDirector is one half of the dominant Australian GP-software duopoly. Its programmatic surface is delivered through Telstra Health Smart API+, a FHIR-native integration gateway that lets approved technology partners exchange data with MedicalDirector Helix (and, on a case-by-case basis, MedicalDirector Clinical) without bespoke, platform-specific integrations. Smart API+ is a gated, partner-onboarded API: it is publicly announced and described but has no self-serve public developer portal, and no FHIR CapabilityStatement or OpenAPI is published anonymously. Access is granted through a partner agreement, and the underlying FHIR version and SMART-on-FHIR auth specifics are not disclosed on public pages.

providers.name: Infinitus
providers.description: Infinitus Systems is a safety-first healthcare voice AI platform that automates outbound and inbound phone calls to patients, payors, and providers for clinical and administrative tasks including benefit verification, prior authorization, prescription follow-up, and patient engagement. Its products include AI Agents (autonomous call handling), AI Copilots (human-assisted tools), Studio (a no-code agent builder), and Lens (conversation analysis and real-time clinical risk detection), backed by a healthcare knowledge graph. Benefit verification can be invoked as individual or bulk requests through an API, and the platform offers a Salesforce integration, though Infinitus does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI. The company is backed by GV and Kleiner Perkins.

providers.name: Vital
providers.description: Vital is a patient-experience technology company for healthcare providers, delivering AI-powered patient guidance and communication across the hospital journey: emergency, inpatient, urgent care, patient access, care coordination, and post-discharge monitoring (Vital Guard). Its software integrates directly with electronic health record systems (Epic, Oracle Health/Cerner, MEDITECH, Veradigm) over FHIR R4 and HL7v2/ADT feeds to surface real-time wait-time predictions, plain-language test-result and discharge-instruction explanations, and AI medical translation. Vital is HIPAA compliant and HITRUST CSF, SOC 2, and NIST CSF aligned. The vitaler.com domain redirects to vital.io; Vital was surfaced as a portfolio company of Threshold Ventures. It exposes EHR/integration surfaces to its hospital customers rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Gradient Health
providers.description: Gradient Health is a multimodal medical data company that accelerates medical AI development by giving AI developers secure, self-service access to diverse, de-identified medical imaging data. Its Atlas platform lets teams search a catalog of 20M+ de-identified imaging studies across hundreds of DICOM tags with longitudinal, patient-level search, construct representative cohorts, and export full DICOM datasets. Gradient Health sources, de-identifies, curates, and delivers data from a network of healthcare data partners, and is HIPAA compliant and AICPA SOC 2 certified. First-party open-source tooling supports cloud-optimized DICOM storage, parsing, and TensorFlow decode operations.

providers.name: OpenFin
providers.description: OpenFin — now branded HERE — is the operating-system layer for enterprise financial desktops. Its container/runtime lets web applications run as secure, interoperable desktop apps, adding Workspace surfaces (Home, Dock, Store, Notifications Center, Browser) and FDC3-based application interop. The developer surface is a JavaScript `fin` runtime/container API (with Java and .NET adapters and a rich set of @openfin npm packages), not a REST/HTTP API. OpenFin is deployed across banks and financial institutions and is backed by Bain Capital Ventures. This profile was enriched from OpenFin/HERE's public developer surface.

providers.name: Axxess
providers.description: Home health, hospice, and private duty software with REST APIs for managing patient plans of care, visit documentation, billing, scheduling, and OASIS assessments. Axxess provides certified EHR technology with FHIR-compliant interoperability, supporting data exchange across care settings via HL7, TEFCA, FHIR, HITRUST, and HIPAA standards.

providers.name: Birdie
providers.description: Birdie is a UK homecare technology platform that gives domiciliary care agencies a single unified system for care management, rostering and scheduling, finance and invoicing, quality and compliance, medication management and clinically-validated assessments, backed by dedicated apps for carers and families. Over 1,000 homecare providers use Birdie to save time, reduce mistakes and evidence care quality, with a Q-Score that predicts CQC ratings in real time. Birdie is UK-hosted and holds ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials Plus and NHS Data Security and Protection Toolkit assurances. It is backed by Index Ventures. Birdie does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI specification; this profile captures its identity, domain security and compliance posture.

providers.name: Forus
providers.description: Forus (formerly Tandem) is an AI-powered healthcare technology company operating a network that connects physicians, pharmacies, payers, and biopharmaceutical companies to accelerate patient access to prescribed medicines. Its platform automates the administrative work between a clinical decision and treatment initiation: insurance prior authorization, AI-generated denial appeals, financial-assistance enrollment, benefit verification, and pharmacy fulfillment routing. Forus is embedded in physician workflows across most U.S. zip codes and is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant. It offers no public developer API, OpenAPI spec, or SDKs; this profile captures the company's public web, trust, and security surface.

providers.name: Waystar
providers.description: Waystar is a healthcare payments and revenue cycle management (RCM) software company that operates a national clearinghouse connecting providers to payers. Its cloud platform spans financial clearance (eligibility, prior authorization, patient estimation), claim management, payment and remittance management, and denial prevention and recovery. Waystar exposes integration through REST APIs, web services, HL7, sFTP/batch, RPA, and X12 EDI transactions (270/271 eligibility, 276/277 claim status, 837 claims, 835 remittance/ERA, 278 authorization). API access is delivered through a partner/developer program at developer.waystar.com; detailed endpoint specifications, sandbox credentials, and authentication (HMAC-SHA256 / OAuth 2.0) are gated behind registration and a signed partnership, so the API surface below is modeled from Waystar's public product and developer-portal descriptions and the underlying X12 standards rather than from a published OpenAPI definition.

providers.name: Garmin
providers.description: Garmin is the global leader in GPS-enabled wearables, cycling computers, outdoor handhelds, marine electronics, aviation avionics, and automotive navigation. Garmin's developer surface spans the Connect IQ wearable app platform (Monkey C, watch faces, data fields, widgets, device apps), the Garmin Connect Developer Program cloud APIs (Health, Activity, Women's Health, Training, Courses), the Health SDK for direct BLE streaming from wearables, the FIT SDK that defines the industry's de-facto endurance data interchange format, Navionics marine cartography, inReach satellite messaging, the ANT/ANT+ wireless protocol, and specialized APIs for golf, aviation flight data, fleet telematics, and custom outdoor maps.

providers.name: Quartet Health
providers.description: Quartet Health is a value-based behavioral healthcare enablement and delivery platform that identifies, engages, and connects patients with mental health services across 39 states. It serves health plans, health systems, and community mental health centers with care coordination, patient-to-provider matching, and direct delivery of behavioral health care through its own medical group, focused on whole-person care for individuals with serious mental illness and other behavioral health needs. Quartet was acquired by NeuroFlow. Added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences company profile; the public site exposes no developer or API surface, but does publish a substantive security and compliance program.

providers.name: Enzyme
providers.description: Enzyme is a cloud-based electronic Quality Management System (eQMS) for the life sciences, serving medical device, digital health, and biopharma companies. The platform is 21 CFR Part 11 compliant and validated out-of-box, spanning the full product lifecycle: document control, change control, and training as core functions; design control, risk management, and supplier management for premarket; and audits, complaints, nonconformance, and CAPA for postmarket. It integrates with enterprise tools including Microsoft Office 365, Slack, Salesforce, Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Google Workspace, and Jenkins, and is designed to scale from startup through IPO-stage organizations. Enzyme was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC (Data Collective) and was acquired by Greenlight Guru.

providers.name: Journey Clinical
providers.description: Journey Clinical is a telehealth platform for ketamine-assisted psychotherapy (KAP). It pairs licensed medical prescribers who manage patient eligibility, prescribing, and clinical monitoring with a member network of independent licensed psychotherapists who deliver the preparation, dosing, and integration therapy sessions. Alongside KAP the company offers standalone medication management and Spravato (esketamine) treatment, operates across 25+ US states, and accepts major insurance plans as well as HSA/FSA payment. Journey Clinical is a HIPAA-covered telehealth provider (publishing a Notice of Privacy Practices) and, as surfaced through the API Evangelist network, does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal. This profile captures its public identity, compliance posture, and domain security as a company record.

providers.name: Klara
providers.description: Klara is a US healthcare patient-engagement and communication platform, now part of Modernizing Medicine (ModMed), that gives medical practices two-way secure messaging, patient texting, appointment reminders and scheduling, intake and forms, telemedicine, and automated workflow tools to reduce phone volume and staff workload. Klara markets integration with 50+ EHR and practice-management systems, but it does not publish its own self-serve public developer API, FHIR CapabilityStatement, or downloadable OpenAPI. Its parent, ModMed, operates a partner-gated developer program at portal.api.modmed.com covering an ONC-certified HL7 FHIR R4 API with SMART-on-FHIR (built for the 21st Century Cures Act, US Core, OAuth2, bulk NDJSON export) plus a proprietary FHIR API for the EMA and gGastro EHR/PM platforms and a Synapsys App Marketplace. That certified API surface belongs to ModMed's EHR products, not to the Klara messaging product itself. Home market is the United States.

providers.name: Lingco Language Labs
providers.description: Lingco Language Labs, Inc. is a Delaware-incorporated education technology company operating Lingco Classroom, a cloud language-learning platform used by schools and universities. Lingco pairs a library of pre-built, customizable world-language content with an instructor platform for building courses, assigning activities and tracking learner outcomes. Lingco publishes no general-purpose public developer API; its integration surface is standards-based education interoperability: an IMS/1EdTech LTI 1.3 tool (OIDC third-party-initiated login, JWKS, Assignment and Grade Services and Names and Role Provisioning Services) hosted at class.lingco.io, OneRoster v1.1 rostering via REST or SFTP CSV, a Canvas API client integration, and SSO with Google Classroom, Schoology and Clever.

providers.name: Sword
providers.description: Sword Health is a digital health company delivering AI-powered virtual care for musculoskeletal (MSK) pain, pelvic health, and injury prevention. Founded in 2015 in Portugal by Virgilio Bento, Sword pairs licensed physical therapists with motion-sensor and computer-vision technology so members can complete clinically supervised physical therapy from home. Its platform spans an enrollment platform, a treatment platform, a mobile application backed by a mobile API, a file-exchange platform for enterprise clients, and an AI care system. Sword serves 1,000+ enterprise and health-plan clients across three continents, is backed by investors including General Catalyst, Khosla Ventures, Founders Fund, and Transformation Capital, and maintains SOC 2 Type 2, HITRUST, ISO 13485, HIPAA, GDPR, and Cyber Essentials compliance. Sword does not currently publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its identity, status, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Celer Network
providers.description: Celer Network is a blockchain interoperability protocol that enables seamless cross-chain experiences for dApps, assets, and users. Its flagship cBridge is a decentralized cross-chain asset bridge supporting 40+ blockchains with over $14B in cumulative transfer volume, and Celer IM (Inter-chain Messaging) is a framework for building multi-blockchain applications with efficient liquidity, coherent logic, and shared state. For developers, the cBridge gateway exposes a public gRPC-Web / REST API (sgn.gateway.v1.Web) for discovering supported chains and tokens, estimating cross-chain transfer fees, tracking transfer status, and withdrawing liquidity. Celer was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Stack Health
providers.description: Stack Healthcare (stackhealthcare.com) is a health-insurance fintech offering affordable, flexible coverage for small businesses and their teams. Operating as a technology company rather than a bank, Stack acts as a HIPAA Business Associate to employer-sponsored health plans, processing Protected Health Information for enrollment and benefits administration, and partners with Stripe for payments and Celtic Bank for issuing commercial cards. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Stack publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface — the product is a waitlist-gated web application — so this profile captures the identity, security, and compliance posture that is publicly verifiable.

providers.name: Standardization
providers.description: Standardization is the process of implementing and developing technical standards based on the consensus of different parties, including firms, users, interest groups, standards organizations, and governments. The goal is to establish uniform engineering or technical criteria, methods, processes, and practices. Key standards bodies include ISO (International Organization for Standardization), IEEE, IETF, W3C, OASIS, and national bodies such as ANSI, BSI, and DIN. In the API space, standardization covers OpenAPI Specification (OAS), AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, REST, GraphQL, gRPC, and emerging protocols including MCP. Proper standardization reduces legal and operational risk while supporting audit readiness, interoperability, and long-term maintainability.

providers.name: Becton Dickinson
providers.description: Becton Dickinson (BD) is a global medical technology company that develops, manufactures, and sells medical devices, instrument systems, and reagents. In October 2025, BD launched the BD Incada Connected Care Platform, an AI-enabled, cloud-based platform built on AWS that unifies data from nearly 3 million connected BD devices including infusion pumps, patient monitors, and pharmacy robotics. BD also produces the Pyxis medication management system and integrates with EMRs via HL7 FHIR standards for clinical data exchange.

providers.name: Cyberpsyc
providers.description: CyberPsyc Software Solutions, operating as WellTrack Boost (now part of ProtoCall Services), builds self-guided, clinically-supported digital cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) tools for behavioral health and wellness. The platform lets users assess and understand their mental health on their own devices and schedule through MoodCheck mood tracking, the Zen Room, a Thought Diary, an Activity Scheduler, Fun and Achievement planning, and guided modules for stress, anxiety, and depression. WellTrack Boost is deployed by college counseling centers and certified community behavioral health clinics, offering institutional single sign-on through a SAML integration surface. No public developer REST API or OpenAPI is currently published.

providers.name: Ambience
providers.description: Ambience Healthcare builds an AI operating system for healthcare that reduces clinician administrative burden and protects revenue integrity at the point of care. Its ambient AI platform performs real-time medical encounter transcription, clinical note generation, integrated clinical documentation improvement (CDI) with ICD-10 coding suggestions, and EHR patient-context enrichment across more than 100 specialties in outpatient, emergency, and inpatient settings. The platform integrates directly with major EHRs including Epic, Oracle Cerner, and athenahealth. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in San Francisco, Ambience is backed by roughly $370M in funding, including a $243M Series C co-led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Oak HC/FT. Ambience exposes a gated Integration API (documentation and access granted on request via emr-integration@ambiencehealthcare.com) rather than a public self-serve developer program.

providers.name: Archy
providers.description: Archy is an all-in-one, cloud-based dental practice management platform that consolidates scheduling, clinical charting, imaging, insurance verification, billing, patient communication, online payments, and reporting into a single system, layered with AI agents (Scribe for clinical notes, Revenue for insurance claim posting, Intelligence for analytics, and Verify for real-time insurance verification) that automate routine practice workflows. Founded in 2021 by Jonathan Rat and Benjamin Kolin and backed by TCV, Bessemer Venture Partners, CRV, and Entree Capital, Archy has raised roughly $47M through a 2025 Series B and serves tens of thousands of active users across dental practices. As a handler of protected health information it is HIPAA-compliant, publishes a Vanta-hosted trust center, and ships native iOS and Android apps. Archy exposes no public developer API; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network for identity, security, and discoverability coverage.

providers.name: Clara 2
providers.description: Clara is an AI-powered primary care and longevity practice, founded by the team behind Circle Medical and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and A.Capital. Clara pairs deep clinical AI with board-certified clinician review: it securely imports and analyzes a patient's medical records, surfaces health trends, assists with symptom assessment, medication refills, lab ordering, and longevity/biomarker goals, and routes every medical recommendation to a licensed clinician for review and approval before it reaches the patient. The company operates as a fully licensed primary care practice across all 50 U.S. states and is a HIPAA-covered entity. Clara is a consumer telehealth product (subscription plans on askclara.com) and currently publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity, trust, and compliance surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Disclo
providers.description: Disclo is a workplace-accommodations software platform that powers end-to-end management of ADA, FMLA, and state-leave requests, medical-certification verification, and the interactive accommodation process for employers. The HIPAA- and SOC 2-compliant portal automates accommodation workflows and compliance documentation, adds AI-assisted medical-certification review (Disclo Verify) and candidate accommodations for recruiting (Disclo Hire), and integrates with 50+ HRIS and ATS systems. Disclo is a private B2B SaaS company backed by Bain Capital Ventures and General Catalyst; it operates a secure customer portal (secure.disclo.com) and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI. Access is enterprise, demo/sales-led rather than self-serve.

providers.name: Mabel
providers.description: Mabel is a healthcare technology company (Irvine, California; backed by 500 Global) that helps Medicare accountable care organizations (ACOs) enroll and engage beneficiaries. Its platform is a market leader in voluntary alignment, used by roughly one in three ACOs, and spans four core solutions: Voluntary Alignment (campaign execution, response processing, analytics, and compliance auditing for LEAD, ACO REACH, and GUIDE programs), Health Surveys (social determinants of health screenings, NPS, and custom surveys with CMS-formatted reporting), Beneficiary Notifications (compliance notices via email, mail, or SMS with audit-ready tracking), and Letters From Your Doctor (provider-based outreach for enrollment, surveys, and appointments). Mabel is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified. No public developer API or SDK surface is published at this time; this profile captures the company's identity, compliance posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Nilo Health
providers.description: Nilo Health (nilo.health) is a Berlin-based employee mental health platform that helps businesses support their workforce's mental well-being. Founded in 2019 by Ines Raeth, Catalina Turlea and Jonas Keil, nilo gives teams access to 500+ psychologists for 1:1 video counseling in 50+ languages, alongside self-guided digital programs, group roundtables, and an HR analytics dashboard. It is delivered to employers as a company benefit (SaaS) rather than through a public developer API; there is no published developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time. nilo integrates with HR platforms such as Personio and Lano via partner marketplaces, and publishes a trust center citing ISO/IEC 27001. The company is backed by Speedinvest and was added to the API Evangelist network as a Speedinvest portfolio company.

providers.name: Pelago
providers.description: Pelago is a virtual-first digital clinic for substance use disorder, delivering personalized treatment for tobacco, alcohol, opioid, cannabis, and stimulant use. The platform combines digital cognitive behavioral tools, live clinical counseling, and medication-assisted treatment (PelagoRX) with same-day nationwide access. Pelago sells primarily to employers and health plans as a covered behavioral-health benefit, and also serves adolescents and members with co-occurring mental-health and chronic conditions. Formerly known as Quit Genius, the company is backed by Atomico and EQT Ventures. It publishes a public marketing and member-enrollment web presence but exposes no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and published security/compliance posture.

providers.name: Rivet Health
providers.description: Rivet Health is a cloud-based revenue cycle management (RCM) platform for healthcare providers, spanning practices, specialty groups, and hospitals. Its software brings together three core modules: Revenue Diagnostics (AI-driven revenue forecasting, real-time reporting, and denial prevention), Payer Performance (contract management, payer benchmarking, and fee-schedule administration), and Patient Pricing (automated patient cost estimates and No Surprises Act Good Faith Estimates). Rivet describes itself as an agnostic platform that integrates with 30+ practice-management systems, EHRs, and clearinghouses — including Epic, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, AdvancedMD, Veradigm, ModMed, Greenway Health, Nextech, Availity, and Change Healthcare. The company is backed by Menlo Ventures. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference documentation; integrations are delivered through its partner network. Rivet publishes a trust center documenting SOC 2 and HIPAA posture.

providers.name: Alaffia
providers.description: Alaffia (Alaffia Health) is a New York City-based healthtech company building an AI platform that helps health plans reduce improper payments and administrative waste across claims operations. The platform pairs expert clinicians with transparent, traceable AI agents to automate routine clinical case reviews, normalize and extract data from medical records, and align clinical analysis with payer policy while keeping a human validation step. Alaffia targets three operational teams inside payers: payment integrity, utilization management, and appeals, offered as AI agents plus managed services. The company reports outcomes such as 20x throughput, 97%+ accuracy, and 5x ROI, and operates under HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II, and HITRUST compliance. Founded by TJ Ademiluyi (CEO) and Adun Akanni (COO), Alaffia raised a $55M Series B in February 2026 and is backed by FirstMark, Anthemis, and Transformation Capital. Alaffia currently exposes no public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and compliance program.

providers.name: Lassie
providers.description: Lassie is a Swedish insurtech that sells preventive digital pet insurance for dogs and cats. Founded in Stockholm in 2020, the company pairs veterinary-care cover with an app-based prevention programme: owners take courses designed by animal experts and earn up to SEK 500 a year off their premium. Cover includes unlimited digital vet consultations through FirstVet, 24-hour claims handling, direct settlement with clinics, no breed or age restrictions and no lock-in period. Lassie AB is an insurance intermediary supervised by Finansinspektionen under the Swedish Insurance Distribution Act (2018:1219); policies are underwritten by Dina Forsakring AB. The company operates in Sweden, Germany and France with 100+ staff and more than one million insured animals, and is backed by a16z and Balderton Capital. Lassie publishes no public developer API - its GraphQL backend at api.lassie.co is private to its own apps - but it does publish a per-market llms.txt, making it an early example of a consumer insurer building an agent-readable surface without an API programme.

providers.name: Abridge
providers.description: Abridge provides enterprise-grade generative AI for clinical conversations, transforming patient-clinician interactions into contextually aware, clinically useful, and billable AI-generated notes. Its Contextual Reasoning Engine powers ambient documentation embedded directly in the Epic EHR (Abridge Inside), with deployments across more than 100 health systems including Mayo Clinic, UPMC, Kaiser Permanente, Johns Hopkins, and Duke Health. Abridge reaches third-party developers and EHR partners through Epic's Partners and Pals program rather than a public, self-service developer API.

providers.name: Soylent
providers.description: Soylent is a nutrition company known for its plant-based, complete-nutrition meal-replacement drinks, powders, and bars, sold direct-to-consumer through its Shopify-powered online store at soylent.com. It reached the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of a16z and GV. Soylent publishes no traditional developer program, but its storefront is agent-native: it implements the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) with a live MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search, cart, and buyer-approved checkout; publishes /llms.txt and /agents.md agent instructions; and exposes Shopify Customer Account OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect authentication with a discoverable authorization server. This profile captures that agent-commerce and authentication surface.

providers.name: Flinn
providers.description: Flinn (flinn.ai) is an AI-powered regulatory and quality platform for medical technology and in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) manufacturers. It automates post-market surveillance (PMS) and compliance obligations across global frameworks including the EU MDR, IVDR, and FDA 21 CFR requirements. The platform continuously monitors 15+ safety databases in a single click, performs AI-assisted literature evaluation, automates complaint handling, and generates audit-ready reports for low- to high-risk medical devices. Flinn is used by 200+ global MedTech and IVD organizations, is hosted exclusively on AWS in Frankfurt (eu-central-1) with data kept inside the EU, and is validated/certified against ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/TR 80002-2, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, FDA 21 CFR Part 11, the EU AI Act, and GDPR. Backed by HV Capital and Speedinvest. This profile has been enriched from Flinn's public web presence; the product is a closed SaaS application with no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Sworkit
providers.description: Sworkit Health is a digital wellbeing platform combining on-demand fitness, mindfulness, mobility and recovery, nutrition, and wellness challenges to help organizations improve employee engagement and workforce health. Rather than a public REST API, Sworkit exposes its workout content to developers through the Sworkit Workout Player Platform — an embeddable web player and a React Native mobile SDK component, both published on npm under the @sworkit org. Its security and compliance posture covers SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, and GDPR.

providers.name: Glass Health
providers.description: Glass Health is a San Francisco-based clinical AI company founded in 2021 by Dereck Paul (CEO) and Graham Ramsey (Head of Product) that builds an AI clinical decision support (CDS) and ambient scribing co-pilot for physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, residents, and medical students. The Glass platform combines large language model reasoning with curated, physician-reviewed clinical guidelines to generate ranked differential diagnoses, evidence-based assessment and plans, chart summaries, and direct answers to clinical questions ("Consult"), all delivered with inline citations. Glass also provides ambient scribing that listens during patient encounters and generates History and Physical notes, progress notes, discharge summaries, and patient-facing instructions, plus EHR integration via SMART on FHIR to pull demographics, problem lists, medications, laboratory values, vital signs, imaging, and encounter data into the workflow. Glass offers a tiered SaaS plan (Lite free tier, Starter at $20/month, Pro at $90/month, Max at $200/month) along with iOS and Android apps, and a public Glass Developer API ($250/month minimum, token-metered beyond the floor) that exposes the same clinical AI agent — Consult, Differential Diagnosis, Assessment and Plan, and Scribing endpoints — for third-party healthcare products. Glass is backed by Breyer Capital and graduated from Y Combinator's W23 batch, with roughly $6.5M in total disclosed funding. The provider does not publish an open OpenAPI specification or open-source SDKs; integration details are gated behind the developer portal and an enterprise contact at enterprise@glass.health.

providers.name: Lively
providers.description: Lively is a fintech-healthtech company that provides modern, cloud-based Health Savings Accounts (HSA) alongside Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA), Health Reimbursement Arrangements (HRA), COBRA, and commuter benefits for individuals, families, employers, benefits administrators, and third-party administrators. Lively pairs interest-bearing and investment-enabled HSAs (via a Schwab Health Savings Brokerage Account and a guided HSA portfolio) with an employer dashboard for contributions and administration, positioning itself around transparent, zero-hidden-fee pricing. Backed by Costanoa Ventures and GGV Capital, Lively integrates with benefit administration platforms and third-party administrators but does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; integration is handled through its sales and partnerships channels. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Lively's public web surface.

providers.name: Quant Network
providers.description: Quant Network is a blockchain interoperability company whose Overledger platform provides APIs to issue, connect, and monitor digital assets, smart contracts, transactions, and accounts across multiple distributed ledger technologies without requiring blockchain expertise.

providers.name: Ultralight
providers.description: Ultralight is an AI-native electronic health record (EHR) and operating system for functional, integrative, and longevity medicine practices. The platform brings clinical data, workflows, and intelligence into a single system, synthesizing wearable data, longitudinal symptoms, labs, and treatment history with a built-in, clinician-reviewed clinical intelligence layer, alongside a consumer-grade patient app, automated workflows, and HIPAA-compliant infrastructure. Ultralight is headquartered in San Francisco and backed by Anthemis through its Female Innovators Lab. The company publishes no public developer or API surface today.

providers.name: CVS Health
providers.description: CVS Health is a Fortune 50 healthcare services and retail pharmacy company. Its core operating units include CVS Pharmacy (retail pharmacy and mail-order), CVS Caremark (pharmacy benefit management / PBM), Aetna (health insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, dental and vision), MinuteClinic (walk-in clinics), Oak Street Health (primary care for Medicare patients), and Signify Health (in-home health evaluations). CVS Health does not currently operate a public developer portal or generally available REST API. Programmatic integrations with CVS Pharmacy, Caremark, and Aetna are typically established through business partnership agreements, EDI / NCPDP pharmacy networks, and HIPAA-aligned interoperability channels (e.g., FHIR endpoints exposed to qualifying healthcare partners under regulatory mandates such as the CMS Interoperability Rule). Developer-facing artifacts in this index are limited to public marketing, corporate, and digital health references.

providers.name: Lena Health
providers.description: Lena Health is a Houston, Texas healthcare technology company founded in the Texas Medical Center that combines AI agents with human care navigators to deliver care coordination at scale. Its LenaConnect platform handles routine patient outreach calls, appointment scheduling and coordination, payer and provider hold times, automatic call documentation, EHR integration, and resource and referral management, so human navigators can focus on building trust with patients. Lena offers fully managed care navigation services covering Chronic Care Management (CCM), Transitional Care Management (TCM), rising-risk care management, and annual wellness visits, and works with health plans, accountable care organizations (ACOs), health systems, provider groups, care management providers, and community organizations. The company reports retrospective matched-cohort results of 29% fewer unplanned readmissions, 42% fewer ED visits, and $3,116 saved per patient within 180 days. Lena Health is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, and publishes a trust center. Lena Health is a Techstars portfolio company. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment; the platform is delivered as a managed service with EHR integration handled through engagements.

providers.name: Zoetis
providers.description: Zoetis is the world's leading animal health company, dedicated to discovering, developing, manufacturing, and commercializing medicines, vaccines, diagnostics, and technologies for animals. The company operates in over 100 countries and provides digital connectivity solutions that integrate veterinary diagnostics, reference laboratory services, and practice management systems through the Vetscan platform, enabling bidirectional communication between point-of-care analyzers and veterinary practice information management systems (PIMS).

providers.name: Agilemd
providers.description: AgileMD is a clinical decision support company that embeds real-time predictive analytics and evidence-based clinical pathways directly into hospital electronic health record (EHR) workflows such as Epic and Cerner. Its FDA-cleared eCART Clinical Deterioration Suite continuously scores patient risk from nearly 100 real-time variables — labs, vital signs, and nursing assessments — to help care teams recognize deteriorating patients earlier, while its Clinical Pathways product standardizes evidence-based order sets, documentation, and protocols across care settings. AgileMD is used across 400+ hospitals by more than 150,000 clinical users and has processed millions of patient encounters. The company is backed by Y Combinator, MATTER, and Rock Health.

providers.name: Aidoc
providers.description: Aidoc is a clinical artificial intelligence company whose aiOS platform runs, orchestrates, and governs FDA-cleared clinical AI across health systems. Its modules span radiology, cardiology, neurovascular, and vascular care — detecting acute findings (stroke, pulmonary embolism, brain aneurysm, incidental findings) and coordinating care teams at the point of care. aiOS is a vendor-neutral platform that runs both Aidoc and third-party algorithms and integrates into existing hospital IT stacks (PACS, EHR, mobile) using standard healthcare interoperability protocols (DICOM, HL7, FHIR) rather than a public developer REST API. Aidoc reports adoption across more than 1,600 medical centers worldwide. Surfaced as a general-catalyst portfolio company and enriched here for security posture, interoperability conformance, and identity; no public developer API surface is published.

providers.name: AiVF
providers.description: AIVF develops AI-powered software for in vitro fertilization (IVF) clinics, embryology laboratories, and patients. Its EMA platform applies computer vision and machine learning to embryo evaluation (AIVF Day-3 and Day-5), genetics, outcomes analytics, and clinic-patient communication to improve embryo selection and IVF success rates, alongside ART Compass by AIVF for fertility-lab benchmarking. AIVF holds a CE mark and names ISO 27001, ISO 27799, ISO 13485, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance; in the US an AI component is an investigational device. AIVF was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API — this profile captures the company's identity, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Clipboard Health
providers.description: Clipboard Health (now branded simply "Clipboard", at clipboardworks.com) is a U.S. healthcare workforce marketplace that connects workplaces — long-term care facilities, home health and hospice agencies, hospitals, dental practices, and travel assignments — with vetted, independent professionals to fill open shifts. Workplaces post shifts and Clipboard matches, credentials, schedules, and pays qualified workers, with the platform handling documentation, compliance, and instant pay for pros. The company reports serving more than 6,500 workplaces and over a million workers nationwide. Backed by Initialized Capital and IVP, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. Clipboard Health publishes no public consumer API; its public developer surface is limited to open-source TypeScript utility libraries on npm (the @clipboard-health scope, from github.com/ClipboardHealth/core-utils) and a minimal RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: HealthVerity
providers.description: HealthVerity is a United States life-sciences data platform, headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, that operates what it describes as the nation's largest real-world data (RWD) ecosystem - more than 150 billion de-identified transactions covering over 330 million U.S. patients across 75-plus data sources spanning medical and pharmacy claims, labs, and EHR (following its integration of Symphony Health). Its products are organized around the IPGE framework (Identity, Privacy, Governance, Exchange) and include HealthVerity Marketplace (verified RWD datasets), Identity Manager and Census (privacy-safe probabilistic identity resolution that replaces PII with a universal HealthVerity ID / HVID), Governance Manager, HealthVerity FLOW, and eXOs (an AI-native real-world-evidence agent). HealthVerity is a HIPAA-aligned, tokenization-and-de-identification company serving pharma, payers, and government - not a self-serve, standards-based clinical interoperability vendor. Unlike EHR and FHIR-network players, it exposes no public developer portal, no FHIR CapabilityStatement, and no downloadable OpenAPI; the only vendor-named programmatic surface is the gated, enterprise HealthVerity Identity API for real-time de-identification, described conceptually on the Identity Manager product page but without public reference documentation, base URL, or self-serve onboarding.

providers.name: Workit Health
providers.description: Workit Health is a 100% virtual addiction-treatment provider delivering telehealth care for opioid use disorder, alcohol use disorder, and kratom/7-OH dependence via mobile app and video visits with licensed clinicians. Care includes FDA-approved medications such as Suboxone (buprenorphine/naloxone) and naltrexone, recovery groups, and asynchronous care-team messaging, serving members across fourteen US states. Backed by Insight Partners and Lux Capital. Workit Health publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Tendo
providers.description: Tendo is a healthcare software company founded in 2020 by siblings Dan and Jen Goldsmith (previously of Veeva Systems and Instructure) and headquartered in the Philadelphia area. Tendo builds a cloud, purpose-built healthcare platform and a suite of applications that connect patients, clinicians, providers, and caregivers across the care journey — spanning digital patient engagement, quality and clinical documentation improvement, hospital quality rankings analytics, and the Care Connect marketplace for employers, providers, and patients. The company raised a $50M Series B led by Lux Capital (with General Catalyst). Tendo runs public trust and status surfaces (a SafeBase trust center with SOC 2 and HIPAA, an Atlassian Statuspage) but does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI; API integration is delivered under private partner agreements. Surfaced as a Lux Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: WELL Health Technologies
providers.description: WELL Health Technologies Corp (TSX: WELL, OTCQX: WHTCF) is a Vancouver, Canada-headquartered healthcare technology company that is Canada's largest outpatient medical clinic owner-operator and a leading multi-disciplinary digital health service provider. It runs two synergistic channels: an omni-channel patient services business operating 115+ multidisciplinary clinics across Canada plus US telehealth and anesthesia operations, and a virtual-services / practitioner-enablement platform serving 44,000+ providers through the OSCAR Pro EMR, billing and revenue-cycle tools, eReferral, digital booking, and ePharma. Its programmatic surface is the apps.health marketplace, through which third-party digital health apps integrate with WELL's network of EMRs (OSCAR Pro, Profile) using HL7 FHIR and other interoperability standards. As of this review WELL exposes no self-serve public developer portal, sandbox, OpenAPI, or FHIR CapabilityStatement; integration is FHIR-based but gated behind a partner/contact process. Home market is Canada, positioned in a province-fragmented healthcare landscape coordinated federally by Canada Health Infoway's pan-Canadian FHIR (CA Core / CA Baseline) specifications.

providers.name: AcuityMD
providers.description: AcuityMD is a MedTech commercial intelligence platform that combines precise medical device market data, AI-powered insights (AcuityAI), and workflow tools to help commercial teams accelerate product adoption and revenue growth. Used by 500+ medical device companies, the platform spans Market Intelligence, Care Journeys, Targeting, Pipeline, Contracts, Territories and Forecasting. AcuityMD is a closed enterprise SaaS product: it exposes no public developer API, but integrates via a Salesforce AppExchange app, a Snowflake Marketplace listing, and an enterprise Data Connector that delivers market intelligence into customer data warehouses. Backed by ICONIQ Capital and Redpoint Ventures.

providers.name: Artera
providers.description: Artera is a healthcare technology company providing an AI-powered patient communication and engagement platform used by hospitals, health systems, and medical practices to unify how they reach and care for patients.
