The platform orchestrates SMS, voice, email, and chat across the patient journey — appointment scheduling and reminders, patient intake, payments, referral management, care-gap closure, prescription refills, multilingual engagement, and after-hours call routing and triage — increasingly through agentic AI. Artera connects to the EHR and patient-facing vendors via API, FHIR, and HL7v2 integrations with major systems including Epic, Oracle Health, MEDITECH, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, Veradigm, NextGen, Greenway, ModMed, AdvancedMD, and Netsmart. The company maintains a strong security and compliance posture (SOC 2 Type 2, HITRUST, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701, FedRAMP, HIPAA). It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: MeetAsh
providers.description: Ash (MeetAsh / Ash Wellness) is a New York-based health technology company, founded in 2019, that powers white-label at-home health testing programs for health plans, digital health companies, and public health organizations. Through a single, developer-friendly REST API integration, partners can trigger test kits, manage shipping logistics, and securely transmit results back into an EHR or patient portal across a national network of CLIA- and CAP-certified laboratories. Ash offers 120+ at-home diagnostic panels (hormone, cancer, allergy, STI, chronic condition, and infectious-disease testing with self-collected blood, stool, urine, saliva, and swab samples), care-gap-closure programs for HEDIS measures, kitting and fulfillment, physician-of-record services, and real-time reporting dashboards. The platform is fully HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, with enterprise-grade encryption protecting PHI. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network; the developer documentation is partner-gated (password protected).

providers.name: Dentrix
providers.description: Dentrix is a dental practice management platform from Henry Schein One, used by dental offices to manage patients, scheduling, clinical charting, treatment planning, insurance, and billing. Dentrix exposes third-party integration APIs through two distinct channels. The original Dentrix Developer Program (DDP, launched 2012) targets the on-premise Dentrix desktop application: integrations run locally against the office's Dentrix database over password-protected ODBC connections, stored procedures, table views, and DLL functions (authenticated via a RegisterUser call) - it is NOT a public REST/cloud API, and cloud integrations require a locally installed desktop agent. The newer Dentrix Ascend API Exchange (launched July 2023) is a cloud, REST/JSON API over HTTPS secured with OAuth 2.0 on the SOC 2 Type II Dentrix Ascend platform, exposing patient, scheduling, claims, and inventory data. Both channels are partner-gated: access requires an application, a signed agreement, and paid developer fees. There is no public self-serve API key or published OpenAPI, so the APIs below are modeled from Henry Schein One's public developer materials rather than an official machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Omada Health
providers.description: Omada Health is a virtual-first healthcare company founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Francisco that delivers integrated, evidence-based care programs for chronic disease management. Omada combines one-on-one health coaching, connected smart devices (cellular scales, blood pressure monitors, glucose meters), interactive lessons, and peer communities to support people managing prediabetes, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, high cholesterol, and musculoskeletal (MSK) conditions, along with GLP-1 medication support and weight health. The company sells to employers, health plans, benefit consultants, and health systems rather than to individual consumers directly, and operates as a HIPAA covered entity and business associate. Omada Health is publicly traded and is a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It has no publicly documented developer API surface; this profile captures the company's public identity, security/compliance posture, and operational transparency pages.

providers.name: Vetspire
providers.description: Vetspire is a cloud-based, AI-enabled veterinary practice management (PIMS) platform for animal hospitals and clinics, covering electronic medical records, scheduling, client communications, billing, inventory, labs, and reminders. Vetspire exposes a single public GraphQL API at https://api.vetspire.com/graphql - every action in the product is powered by GraphQL - authenticated with an Authorization API token and organized by veterinary practice domains (Accounts, Clinical, Schedule, Billing, Inventory, Hospital, Lab, Reminders, Conversations, Analytics, Events). The schema exposes 400+ object types, 248 input objects, and 112 enums, with a maximum query depth of 8.

providers.name: Tuva Health
providers.description: Tuva Health, Inc. is a United States healthcare data company behind The Tuva Project, an open-source, warehouse-native data-transformation platform that harmonizes, validates, normalizes, and enriches raw healthcare data - medical and pharmacy claims, EHR clinical data, ADT feeds, and HL7 FHIR sources - into an analytics-ready Core Data Model and a library of Data Marts (AHRQ measures, readmissions, quality measures, chronic conditions, CCSR, pharmacy). It is delivered primarily as a dbt package plus Python utilities (FHIR Inferno) and a family of source connectors that run inside the customer's own cloud data warehouse - Snowflake, Databricks, Google BigQuery, Amazon Redshift, or Microsoft Fabric - rather than as a hosted service. Tuva is not an HTTP or FHIR API vendor: FHIR R4 is a supported input format that Tuva flattens and maps into its Input Layer, not a live FHIR server it operates. The company pairs the open-source project with a commercial Core Platform. Home market is the United States.

providers.name: 9am Health
providers.description: 9amHealth (join9am.com) is a US virtual cardiometabolic clinic delivering specialized care for type 2 diabetes, obesity/weight loss, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol entirely from home. Founded in 2021 in San Diego by mySugr co-founders Frank Westermann and Anton Kittelberger, the company pairs at-home lab test kits, asynchronous and synchronous telehealth visits with obesity specialists, pharmacists, dietitians, and behavioral health experts, mail-order pharmacy for prescriptions including GLP-1 receptor agonists, and optional connected devices such as continuous glucose monitors into individualized care plans. It sells direct to individuals and through employers, health plans, and pharmacy benefit managers. 9amHealth is a consumer and enterprise telehealth brand and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; this profile captures its public web identity for the API Evangelist network. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: House Rx
providers.description: House Rx is a healthcare technology company that equips independent specialty and community clinics to run in-house, medically integrated dispensing pharmacies. Founded in 2021, its cloud platform — built by specialty pharmacists and physicians — supports the full specialty-medication workflow: prior authorization, financial counseling and copay assistance, fulfillment tools, scalable patient outreach and messaging, real-time operational analytics, and EHR integration so physicians and pharmacists collaborate on patient care. House Rx is SOC 2 compliant and backed by First Round, Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, Maverick Ventures, 1984 Ventures, and Character Ventures. House Rx does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: KRY
providers.description: KRY is a Swedish digital healthcare provider headquartered in Stockholm that operates internationally under the Livi brand. It delivers primary care through video and chat consultations with doctors, nurses, psychologists, physiotherapists, dietitians and midwives via its iOS and Android apps, and also runs physical primary care centres (vardcentraler), child health clinics and midwifery clinics across Sweden. KRY operates as Kry in Sweden (kry.se) and Norway (kry.no) and as Livi in the United Kingdom (livi.co.uk) and France (livi.fr). Services span digital consultations, prescription renewal, medical certificates, vaccination and testing, mental health programmes, occupational health for employers, and regional public healthcare contracts. KRY publishes no public developer program, partner API or SDK surface; the platform is consumer- and clinician-facing, so this profile captures the company identity plus its legal and security surface rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Sword Health
providers.description: Sword Health is a digital musculoskeletal (MSK) and virtual physical-therapy company that pairs licensed clinicians with an AI Care platform (programs including Thrive for MSK, Bloom for pelvic and women's health, Move, and Mind for mental health, with the Phoenix AI care specialist and the Sword Intelligence division). Founded in Portugal in 2015, it sells to employers, health plans, and governments rather than to individual developers. As of this enrichment pass Sword Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; its digital surface is member/clinician apps and employer client portals. Real public surfaces captured here are its trust center (SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR), legal pages, newsroom, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Radial Analytics
providers.description: Radial Analytics (Radial) is a Concord, Massachusetts healthcare technology company providing an AI/ML-powered clinical decision-support platform for the value-based care market. Its HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II certified software helps ACOs, hospitals, health systems, payers, and Medicare Advantage plans account for millions of clinical, claims, and quality datapoints to improve patient outcomes while reducing cost of care. Products include Radial Care, ACO Compare, Opportunity Navigator, decision-support modules, care pathways, and TEAM bundles. The company was founded by MIT PhDs Thaddeus Fulford-Jones and Eric Weiss and is backed by Initialized Capital. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: Revel Ai Health
providers.description: RevelAi Health is a healthcare technology company building a conversational AI platform for orthopedic and musculoskeletal care teams. Its AI agent, "kimi," automates patient outreach, triage, clinical documentation, and follow-up across the care episode, supporting value-based care models, quality reporting, and Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROM) collection. The platform offers multilingual population-health outreach across voice, text, and email, ambient clinical documentation, and AI-augmented staffing and task management for ambulatory surgery centers, hospitals and health systems, and physician practices. The company is a Techstars portfolio company and maintains SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance programs. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no public API surface was found.

providers.name: Theator
providers.description: Theator is a surgical intelligence platform that turns minimally invasive surgical video into structured, actionable intelligence. The company processes operative video footage into procedural insights, outcomes data, and surgery-to-text documentation for three audiences: surgeons seeking objective performance feedback, hospital and health-system executives tracking outcomes and efficiency, and revenue-cycle teams improving documentation and coding. Theator is a healthcare technology company backed by Insight Partners and partners with AWS and Oracle Health. It maintains a formal security and compliance posture (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR) published via its trust center. No public first-party developer API, SDK, or documentation surface has been identified; this profile captures the company's public web, trust, and security surface.

providers.name: Siemens Healthineers
providers.description: Siemens Healthineers AG is a German medical technology company (XETRA SHL) covering medical imaging, laboratory diagnostics, point-of-care testing, advanced therapies, and cancer care (following the April 2021 Varian Medical Systems acquisition for USD 16.4 billion). Its digital surface is anchored by the teamplay digital health platform, the Digital Marketplace, syngo.via OpenApps, and the Frontier Development Kit, with developer access offered through a gated teamplay developer portal that exposes APIs for single sign-on, licensing, user roles and permissions, the teamplay receiver plug-in, DICOM image access, customer-specific report submission, and status indicator notifications. No public OpenAPI specifications are published; the API catalog and reference documentation sit behind teamplay developer account authentication.

providers.name: Chefaa
providers.description: Chefaa is Egypt's leading digital pharmacy and pharmacy-benefits platform, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Cairo. Its GPS-enabled, AI-powered consumer app connects more than 1.5 million monthly users with a nationwide network of over 1,500 partner pharmacies, letting patients upload, order, schedule, and refill both insured and non-insured prescriptions with home delivery, medication reminders, and pharmacist chat support. On the B2B side Chefaa operates a full-stack supply layer for pharmacies and corporates — including Chefaa Supply (direct procurement with deferred payment and consolidated delivery) and the Makhazen pharmacy-supply app — plus the Chefaa Prime subscription for SMEs and consumers. Chefaa is a 500 Global portfolio company. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; Chefaa publishes consumer and B2B web/mobile products but does not expose a public developer API program, so the enrichment below is limited to its public web, security, and domain surface.

providers.name: Curebase
providers.description: Curebase is a San Francisco-based clinical trials technology company (founded 2017) that provides a modern, AI-native eClinical platform for sponsors, CROs, biotechs, MedTech companies, and research sites. The platform unifies the full trial lifecycle in one system: ePRO/eCOA (electronic patient-reported and clinical outcome assessments), eConsent (digital informed consent), EDC (electronic data capture), patient recruitment and screening, participant engagement and retention tooling, and site management. Curebase also ships Sitebase, a free eClinical suite for research sites, and Hope, a conversational AI voice agent. It supports decentralized and hybrid trial models natively. Curebase is a private, venture-backed company (Series B led by Industry Ventures; investors include GGV Capital, Acrew, Gilead, and others). It is SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR compliant. Curebase does not publish a public developer API or API documentation; integration is handled through enterprise engagements.

providers.name: Ellipsis Health
providers.description: Ellipsis Health is a healthcare AI company that has established the human voice as a vital sign for mental health, using clinically validated vocal-biomarker technology, natural language processing, and acoustic models to identify, measure, and monitor the severity of depression and anxiety from short samples of natural speech. Its flagship product, Sage, is an emotionally intelligent, agentic AI care manager that conducts 24/7 patient-engagement calls for health plans, health systems, specialty care, and pharma, handling program enrollment, benefits verification, clinical assessments and surveys, and care coordination. Sage is powered by Ellipsis' patented Empathy Engine, trained on millions of live clinical patient calls, and runs on HIPAA and SOC 2 Type 2 compliant infrastructure. Ellipsis Health integrates with health plans and systems such as Cigna, and exposes a private partner API (used by partners like Augmedix) rather than a public developer platform. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, and CVS Health Ventures.

providers.name: Force Therapeutics
providers.description: Force Therapeutics is a healthcare technology company providing a digital patient-engagement and remote-monitoring platform for surgical and musculoskeletal care. The platform delivers personalized patient education, automated collection of Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs), preoperative optimization, postoperative recovery management, direct patient messaging, and actionable clinical insights for hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and private practices. Force integrates with major EHR systems (Epic, Cerner, MEDITECH, NextGen) through the Redox Connection Network and FHIR/HL7-based workflows rather than a public developer API. The platform is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant, hosted on Amazon Web Services, and backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Lighten
providers.description: Lighten Platforms, Inc. is a San Mateo, California healthcare AI company building an AI-native platform for clinical evidence curation from electronic health record (EHR) data. Its 360° EHR Curation Platform reasons over unstructured clinical notes together with structured records to reconstruct complete patient journeys, applying clinically validated quality assurance at the variable, patient, and cohort level rather than relying on model accuracy metrics alone. On top of that curation layer Lighten delivers Apps & Insights for patient finding and HCP targeting, longitudinal patient journeys, and market intelligence, plus a "Beyond Claims" offering that integrates curated EHR signal with claims data for broader coverage. The company serves life sciences, health systems, data and analytics consultancies, and investors, and was founded by Xinkun Nie, PhD. Lighten publishes no public developer API program, SDKs, or developer documentation as of this profile.

providers.name: Lightforce
providers.description: LightForce Orthodontics, Inc. is a Boston-area medical device and digital manufacturing company that produces "generative braces" — fully customized, 3D-printed orthodontic brackets and indirect bonding trays generated from each patient's own tooth anatomy and the treating orthodontist's digital treatment plan. Doctors submit intraoral scans and treatment plans through the LightForce Doctor Portal, LightForce designs and 3D-prints patient-specific LightBracket ceramic and metal appliances, and ships custom IDB trays back to the practice. The company operates as a HIPAA-covered digital workflow: no public developer API or developer portal is published, but the Doctor Portal is fronted by a public OpenID Connect identity surface at id.lightforceortho.com. Backed by Matrix Partners, Kleiner Perkins, and others.

providers.name: Nolla Health
providers.description: Nolla Health is a Norway-born, AI-powered telehealth and dermatology company that entered the U.S. market with a $4.5M seed round led by General Catalyst and set up its headquarters in New York City. After treating more than 50,000 patients in Europe and becoming one of Norway's top-five medical apps, Nolla launched an AI-guided skin and acne care platform across 40+ U.S. states. The service pairs proprietary AI symptom assessment with clinician-in-the-loop oversight: patients complete a guided chat, a licensed U.S. medical provider reviews and approves every diagnosis and prescription, and topical medications are shipped directly to the patient. Nolla operates as a consumer-facing product (per-consultation and a monthly subscription) rather than an API provider, and publicly states HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

providers.name: Ritten
providers.description: Ritten is a cloud-based electronic medical record (EMR) and practice-management platform built specifically for behavioral health and substance-use treatment organizations — detox, residential, PHP/IOP, and outpatient providers. Its browser-based product covers clinical documentation (group and individual notes, AI-assisted charting), scheduling, revenue-cycle management (claims, billing, authorizations), a HIPAA-compliant patient portal, treatment planning, compliance tooling (audit trails, signature routing), and outcomes reporting. Ritten is built for HIPAA-regulated and 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality requirements with role-based access controls and audit logs, and supports operational integrations for e-prescribing, labs, eligibility/billing clearinghouses, and telehealth. Ritten does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI at this time. Backed by 8VC and Threshold Ventures; based in Philadelphia, PA.

providers.name: TELUS Health
providers.description: TELUS Health is the digital-health division of TELUS, one of Canada's largest telecommunications and technology companies, and the country's leading health-IT provider. It operates the PS Suite, Med Access, and cloud-native Collaborative Health Record (CHR) electronic medical records used across Canadian primary care, along with pharmacy management, virtual care, and employer/benefits health services. Its documented public integration surface is the CHR Enterprise API, a GraphQL endpoint secured with RS512-signed JWT bearer tokens that exposes clinic data (patients, appointments, encounters, clinical documents and more) for partner-built add-ons, complemented by the TELUS Patient Chart FHIR R4 implementation guide, a package of 89 published StructureDefinition profiles under the http://telus.com/fhir/patientChart canonical for standards-based patient-record exchange out of TELUS EMRs, and the Omara Health Exchange FHIR interoperability platform. Home market is Canada, where healthcare is province-fragmented and FHIR interoperability is stewarded federally by Canada Health Infoway. Both API surfaces are documented but gated behind a partner or CHR-domain agreement.

providers.name: Carecloud
providers.description: CareCloud (NASDAQ: CCLD, formerly MTBC) is a cloud-based healthcare technology company serving 45,000+ providers with an integrated platform spanning electronic health records (EHR), practice management, revenue cycle management (RCM), patient experience tools, and AI-driven clinical documentation (cirrusAI). Its Connector product delivers healthcare interoperability with FHIR and C-CDA data exchange across labs, EHRs, immunization registries, and diagnostics. CareCloud is Drummond-certified ONC Health IT and Surescripts-certified, publishes HIPAA compliance content, and operates a developer portal (AWS API Gateway) at developer.carecloud.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: nference
providers.description: nference is a healthcare-AI company that builds an agentic intelligence layer for clinical research and drug development. Its nSights platform aggregates and analyzes de-identified multimodal patient data at massive scale — 1.4 billion+ clinical notes, 10 billion+ radiology images, 20 million+ digitized pathology whole-slide images, 12 million+ ECG waveforms, and 100 million+ echocardiogram videos — extracting 30,000+ clinical biomarkers to help life-sciences and health-system partners design patient cohorts, explore patient journeys, annotate data for model development, and run advanced data-science workflows across cardiology, oncology, immunology, rare diseases, neurology, infectious diseases, and nephrology. nference spun out the venture companies Anumana (ECG-based biomarker discovery) and Pramana (digital pathology). The company operates as an enterprise B2B platform with no public self-serve API; it is profiled here for its security, compliance, and governance posture. Backed by Matrix Partners.

providers.name: Virta Health
providers.description: Virta Health is a virtual, nutrition-first healthcare company delivering sustainable weight loss and type 2 diabetes reversal. Its program combines personalized nutrition plans, continuous expert health coaching, physician-led medication management, and connected devices, delivered through a consumer mobile app and sold to employers, health plans, and healthcare providers. Virta is HITRUST- and SOC 2 Type II-certified and operates as a HIPAA-covered clinical service. As of this enrichment pass Virta publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification surface; this profile captures its public identity, security posture, and compliance certifications.

providers.name: Carepatron
providers.description: Carepatron is a cloud-based healthcare practice management and EHR platform for therapists, counselors, psychologists, health coaches, nutritionists, and other practitioners. It brings client records, appointment scheduling and online booking, telehealth, AI-assisted clinical notes and documentation, and billing/invoicing with insurance claims into one workspace, and markets HIPAA/SOC/GDPR compliance across 100,000+ clinicians in 120+ countries. As of this review Carepatron does NOT publish a documented public developer API - its pricing page lists "API (coming soon)" on the Advanced plan, and there is no developer portal, API reference, published base URL, OpenAPI definition, or SDK. Third-party connectivity today is limited to a handful of native integrations (Zoom, accounting software, Google Tag Manager). The APIs listed below are logical/product-area groupings modeled from Carepatron's own feature set; their endpoints are NOT documented and are marked as modeled, not confirmed.

providers.name: Commure
providers.description: Commure is a San Francisco-based AI-native healthcare technology company that operates an integrated clinical and operational platform for United States health systems following its 2023 combination with Athelas. Its products span Ambient AI clinical documentation (Scribe/Dictation), end-to-end Revenue Cycle Management (RCM), Call Center Agents, referral Orchestrator, patient Engage coordination, Commure Pro clinical intelligence, Strongline staff-safety alerting, and Athelas Home point-of-care diagnostics, integrating with 60+ EHRs across 130+ health systems processing over $25B in annual claims. Commure launched a FHIR-native open developer platform in 2020, but that public developer portal (developer.commure.com) is no longer live; today the API surface is a gated, partner-only offering governed by a Developer User Agreement (Sandbox Environment + Developer Services), with no self-serve public API documentation, FHIR CapabilityStatement, or downloadable OpenAPI currently published. Home market is the United States.

providers.name: Margo
providers.description: Margo is a Linux Foundation open standard initiative for interoperability at the edge of industrial automation ecosystems. Founded by ABB, Capgemini, Microsoft, Rockwell Automation, Schneider Electric, and Siemens, it defines mechanisms for interoperability between edge applications, devices, and orchestration software.

providers.name: Parachute Health
providers.description: Parachute Health is the leading digital platform for durable medical equipment (DME), home medical equipment, and medical supply ePrescribing. Clinicians eSign and submit DME orders in seconds, and the platform coordinates in real time across a network of 3,000+ supplier locations, 270,000+ eSigning clinicians, and 70,000+ facilities in all 50 states. Parachute integrates with EHR/EMR systems (athenahealth, PointClickCare, Epic, and others) using HL7 2.x and FHIR interfaces, and offers prior-authorization automation, health-plan workflows, and value-based-care coordination. Integration is delivered as private, partner-provisioned EMR/HL7/FHIR interfaces rather than a public self-service developer API.

providers.name: Aware Health
providers.description: Aware Health is an AI-powered musculoskeletal (MSK) care platform that helps employers, health plans, and brokers reduce MSK spend while preventing orthopedic surgeries and chronic pain. The company pairs licensed clinicians (physical therapists and health coaches) with an AI "Predict" engine to triage, navigate, and manage musculoskeletal conditions virtually, and reports reducing MSK costs by roughly 30%. Its platform spans MSK care, chronic care, surgery decision support, member navigation, analytics, and an employer dashboard, delivered via web and an iOS app. Aware Health is a Techstars portfolio company and has raised seed funding (including a $3M round led by Boomerang VC with Bright Ventures). This profile was enriched from the company's public web surface; Aware Health does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Cleerly
providers.description: Cleerly is a digital healthcare company building an AI-powered platform for the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease (heart disease). Its software analyzes coronary CT angiography (CCTA) imaging to automatically quantify and characterize atherosclerotic plaque, measure stenosis severity, and stage disease, giving physicians a precise, personalized picture of a patient's heart-disease risk. The goal is to move heart-disease care from symptom-based testing toward direct measurement of plaque, reducing unnecessary invasive procedures while improving diagnostic accuracy. Cleerly operates as an enterprise clinical SaaS delivered to health systems, cardiologists, and imaging centers rather than a public developer API program; it publishes a marketing and clinical-evidence site plus a clinician-facing application (Cleerly Labs) and a public trust center. Cleerly is backed by Battery Ventures and Insight Partners.

providers.name: Equip Health
providers.description: Equip Health is a virtual, evidence-based eating disorder treatment provider founded in 2019 by Kristina Saffran and Erin Parks. Equip delivers 100% remote, insurance-covered care for all eating disorder diagnoses — anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder (BED), ARFID, atypical anorexia, and OSFED — using Family-Based Treatment (FBT) and other evidence-based approaches. Every patient is matched with a five-person care team: a therapist, medical provider, dietitian, family mentor, and peer mentor. Equip serves patients across the United States with no waitlist, publishes an extensive library of clinical and recovery articles, partners with providers and health plans, and operates a patient portal at my.equip.health. This profile catalogs Equip's public web, legal, security, and content surfaces; Equip publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation program at this time.

providers.name: ExaCare AI
providers.description: ExaCare AI is a post-acute and senior care operations platform that applies AI to admissions, referral management, prior authorization, and reimbursement workflows across skilled nursing, home health, hospice, and assisted living providers. It reads inbound referral and admissions packets, extracts clinical and payer data, and automates the back-office work of accepting and reimbursing patients, with integrations into referral platforms, hospital systems, and EHRs. ExaCare is a private company backed by Insight Partners; it ships a customer web application and a Vanta-hosted Trust Center (HIPAA) but publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Halo Health (Symplr)
providers.description: Halo Health, now part of symplr and marketed as symplr Clinical Communications, is a HIPAA-compliant clinical communication and collaboration platform for healthcare organizations. It provides role-based secure messaging, voice communication, critical alert and clinical-alarm notification, and on-call schedule management so care teams can coordinate around patients. The platform integrates with hospital EHR and clinical systems using healthcare interoperability standards - HL7 ADT for patient admit/discharge/transfer events, HL7 ORU for laboratory and radiology results, and SMTP for alerts such as sepsis notifications - rather than through a documented public developer REST API. symplr acquired Halo Health to extend its healthcare operations software portfolio, and the product now sits alongside symplr's broader workforce, compliance, and provider-data solutions.

providers.name: Hello Heart
providers.description: Hello Heart is a digital health company that combines a mobile app, connected blood-pressure monitors, a smart pill box, and the Nia AI assistant (trained on ACC/AHA guidelines) to help people proactively manage cardiovascular health. Sold primarily to employers, health plans, unions, and public-sector benefits programs as a covered heart-health benefit, the platform pairs self-monitoring with clinically-grounded, "safe AI" coaching to lower blood pressure and reduce cardiac risk. Hello Heart is HITRUST CSF certified, SOC 2 Type 2 audited, NIST CSF aligned, and HIPAA compliant, with data encrypted in transit and at rest and stored within U.S. borders. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public identity, security, and compliance posture.

providers.name: Smile Digital Health
providers.description: Smile Digital Health (formerly Smile CDR) is a Toronto-based health interoperability software company and the commercial steward of the open source HAPI FHIR project (the world's most widely deployed Java implementation of the HL7 FHIR standard). Its flagship product, Smile CDR — marketed under the broader Smile Omni portfolio as the OmniVera Health Data Platform — is a FHIR-native clinical data repository and integration platform that ingests HL7 v2.x, CDA, CSV, JSON, XML, and FHIR payloads, normalizes them into FHIR (R4, R5, STU3, DSTU2), and exposes them through a hardened FHIR REST API, SMART on FHIR / OAuth2 / OIDC security, Bulk Data export, Subscriptions, MDM, Terminology Services, CQL-based Quality Measures, and a JSON Admin API. The platform is deployed on-prem and across AWS, Azure, and GCP, with HITRUST v9.4, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and ONC 2015 Edition certifications, and is used by 190+ global customers, including 30+ US payers running CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization (CMS-0057-F) workloads on its CMS Suite. Adjacent Smile Omni product families include OmniCompli (regulatory compliance, including CMS Suite and CMS Concierge), OmniQ (digital quality measures / HEDIS, Intelligence Hub), and OmniConcierge (managed and professional services). The primary developer surface is the FHIR REST API, with per-endpoint auto-generated OpenAPI / Swagger UI at `{baseUrl}/swagger-ui/`, plus a separate JSON Admin API for cluster, module, user, audit, batch job, MDM, and OpenID Connect administration.

providers.name: Oviva
providers.description: Oviva is a European digital health company, founded in 2014, delivering personalized, dietitian-led care for people managing type 2 diabetes, obesity, and other diet-related conditions. It combines a mobile app for logging food, activity, and progress with human coaching from a network of 420+ dietitians, psychologists, and doctors, operating across the UK, Germany, and Switzerland and serving 900K+ people. Oviva is delivered as a regulated digital therapeutic (CE-marked, ISO 27001, NHS DTAC and CQC assessed) rather than through a public developer API; this profile captures its security, compliance, and legal surface. Backed by Partech.

providers.name: Machinify
providers.description: Machinify is an AI-powered healthcare payment integrity platform that streamlines and automates payment processes for health plans. Its products - Coordinate (claims coordination), Subrogate (subrogation management), Audit (payment audit), Pay (payment processing), and Pharmacy (pharmacy payment integrity) - run on a unified data layer that combines claims and medical records, healthcare foundation models trained on billions of data points, and task-specific AI agents with continuous-improvement feedback loops. Machinify reports 85+ customers including 18 of the top 20 US health plans, coverage of 270 million member lives, and more than $6B in annual cost avoidance and recoveries. The company is backed by Battery Ventures and GV. Machinify does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API reference.

providers.name: Md Ally
providers.description: MD Ally is a New York-based digital health company that integrates telehealth into the 911 emergency response system. Its platform lets emergency dispatchers route low-acuity, non-emergency callers to a virtual care tier, connecting patients with telehealth clinicians, in-network resources, and social services instead of dispatching EMS or defaulting to an emergency-room visit. MD Ally works with public safety agencies and payers to expand traditional two-tier dispatch models, reduce unnecessary ambulance transports and ER visits, and improve patient navigation. Backed by General Catalyst and Techstars.

providers.name: Nitra
providers.description: Nitra is an integrated financial and operational platform — an "operating system" — for independent medical practices, unifying business banking, spend management, payments, accounting, capital, and front-desk automation in one system. Its core products include the Nitra Card (a Visa business card with cashback and vendor pricing), NitraMart (a medical-supplies marketplace), BillPay payment processing, accounting integrations (QuickBooks, Nextech), Trina (an AI assistant for phone reception and invoice matching), and capital products such as lending, equipment financing, and insurance factoring. Nitra primarily serves eye care, aesthetics, dental specialty, and fertility practices as well as multi-site groups. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified and HIPAA-aware, holds funds at FDIC-insured banks, and is backed by a16z and Pantera Capital. Nitra publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Aidence
providers.description: Aidence is a radiology AI company founded in Amsterdam in 2015 that builds clinical AI for the lung cancer pathway. Its flagship product, Veye Lung Nodules (now DeepHealth Lung), is a CE-marked AI solution that detects, classifies, quantifies, and measures growth of pulmonary nodules on chest CT scans, and is the AI of choice in NHS England's Targeted Lung Health Checks screening programme. Aidence was acquired by RadNet in 2022 and now operates under the DeepHealth brand; aidence.com redirects to deephealth.com/aidence. The product integrates with hospital systems over DICOM/PACS via the Veye Engine rather than a public developer REST API — no public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published. This profile captures the company's identity plus its probed security and disclosure posture.

providers.name: Attuned Intelligence
providers.description: Attuned Intelligence is a healthcare voice AI company that automates hospital and community health center call centers with supervised, EHR-integrated Voice AI Agents. Its agents answer every patient call instantly and in the caller's language, resolve needs end-to-end (appointment booking, medication refills, triage routing), and provide real-time human oversight with transcripts and reporting so automation stays safe and auditable. Founded in 2024 by leaders from DeepMind, Google Health, AssemblyAI, and DocuSign, the company emerged from stealth in October 2025 with $13M in funding backed by Threshold Ventures, and serves customers including Cambridge Health Alliance and Lowell Community Health Center. The platform is SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant. Attuned publishes no first-party developer/product API; its Wix-hosted marketing site exposes a generic hosted Site MCP endpoint for agentic access to public site content and business details.

providers.name: Basata
providers.description: Basata is a Phoenix-based healthcare AI company building the operational layer for American medical practices. Its AI agents automate back-office administrative work — processing patient referrals, answering phone calls 24/7, and managing faxes and patient communications — while integrating with existing EHR systems so clinical staff can focus on patient care instead of paperwork. Founded in 2024 by Kaled Alhanafi (CEO, formerly Lyft and Cruise), Chetan Patel (co-founder and president, formerly Medtronic), and Vivin Paliath (co-founder and CTO), Basata raised a $21M Series A led by Basis Set Ventures with Cowboy Ventures and PHX Ventures participating (~$24.5M total). The platform is marketed as fully HIPAA-compliant and the company publishes a SOC 2 attestation. Basata does not currently expose a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and web properties.

providers.name: Legacy
providers.description: Legacy is a United States direct-to-consumer male fertility company offering at-home sperm testing and sperm cryopreservation without a clinic visit. Customers order a collection kit online, provide a sample at home, and return it by free overnight shipping to Legacy's CLIA-certified, CLEP-approved laboratory, where results appear in a private client dashboard within 48 hours of receipt. Services span basic, standard, and advanced semen analysis (count, concentration, motility, morphology, and Halosperm sperm DNA fragmentation), STI testing, multi-year sperm storage bundles, and male fertility supplements. Legacy serves people trying to conceive and those preserving fertility ahead of a vasectomy, testosterone therapy, gender-affirming care, cancer treatment, or military deployment, and is in-network with selected insurers and employer fertility benefit programs. Legacy publishes no public developer API; its notable machine-readable surface is a first-party llms.txt written for AI answer engines.

providers.name: Patientdesk.ai
providers.description: Patientdesk.ai (Patientdesk AI, Inc.) is a California-based, Y Combinator-backed company building an AI-native operating system for dental practices. Its 24/7 AI phone receptionist handles inbound and outbound patient calls, appointment scheduling, real-time insurance verification during the call, automated payment collection and debt follow-up, intake, reminders, and lead generation. The product integrates directly with major dental practice management systems (Dentrix, Open Dental, Eaglesoft, Curve Dental, and others) to book patients straight into a clinic's calendar. Patientdesk.ai is HIPAA compliant, follows SOC 2 security standards, supports multiple languages, and is offered on month-to-month contracts. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer/API surface (OpenAPI, docs, SDKs) is currently published; the company exposes a marketing site and a provider-authored llms.txt.

providers.name: RapidClaims
providers.description: RapidClaims is a healthcare revenue-cycle-management (RCM) company building autonomous AI agents for medical coding and claims. Its platform automates medical coding (RapidCode), value-based-care coding and risk adjustment (RapidVBC), denial management and revenue recovery (RapidRecovery), and a unified revenue cycle platform (RapidRCM) for FQHCs, community health centers, ACOs, physician groups, ambulatory surgery centers, hospitals, and management services organizations. The company emphasizes a healthcare-grade security and compliance posture (HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type II, 256-bit encryption). RapidClaims is backed by Accel and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Virgo
providers.description: Virgo builds AI foundation models for gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy, targeting gut-mediated diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer. Its flagship model, EndoDINO, was trained on the largest known endoscopy dataset (130,037 videos / ~3.5 billion frames), and EndoML is the GI-specific tooling environment for building clinical and research workflows on top of it. Virgo Cloud provides video capture and management for endoscopy procedures, while Virgo Trials accelerates clinical trials with automatic data capture, endoscopic scoring, placebo-response prediction, subgroup identification, and AI biomarker discovery. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bevel
providers.description: Bevel is a consumer digital-health application, built by Finerpoint, Inc., that acts as an AI-powered "connected health coach." It consolidates and interprets health data from wearables (Apple Watch, Oura, Garmin, Amazfit) and lab providers (Labcorp, Quest, LifeLabs) into a single view, scoring daily strain, sleep, recovery, stress/energy, nutrition, cycle, biological age and strength training. Its "Bevel Intelligence" layer delivers conversational, research-backed guidance, personalized workout plans and daily check-ins. Bevel is a mobile-first consumer product with no publicly documented developer API; this profile captures its public web, support, roadmap and legal surface. Backed by General Catalyst.

providers.name: Foodvisor
providers.description: Foodvisor is a mobile nutrition platform whose Vision API uses computer vision and AI to identify food items from photographs and return nutritional information including calories, macronutrients, and serving estimates. The Vision API is offered to enterprise developers under a commercial agreement.

providers.name: Wheel
providers.description: Wheel is a healthcare technology company providing the infrastructure for modern telehealth. Its Wheel Horizon platform is a modular care-enablement system that combines a nationwide clinician network, evidence-based virtual care programs, and integrated clinical operations so digital health companies, health plans, retailers and pharmacies, and life-sciences organizations can launch and scale virtual care. Wheel also operates WheelX, an enterprise AI health exchange, and Connected Services for integration. Wheel exposes a partner API, governed by an API Terms of Use and gated behind an approval process; the platform is HIPAA compliant and maintains SOC 2 controls. Public API reference documentation, SDKs, and a developer portal are not published. Wheel was surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV.

providers.name: Findoctave
providers.description: Findoctave (operating as Octave) is a mental health care provider offering virtual and in-person therapy across 20+ U.S. states. Services include individual, couples, and family therapy, DBT, and specialized centers of excellence for perinatal and postpartum health, LGBTQIA+ (queer resiliency), trauma, and women's emotional health. Octave is in-network with major insurers (Aetna, Blue Shield of California, BCBS plans, Health Net, and others) and publishes a therapist directory, cost calculator, and getting-started flow through its consumer website. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Felicis and added to the API Evangelist network; Octave exposes no public developer API, so this profile is a company identity record rather than an API listing.

providers.name: FirstVet
providers.description: FirstVet is a digital veterinary care company offering 24/7 online video consultations with licensed veterinarians for dogs, cats, and other pets. Founded in Sweden, FirstVet operates a consumer telehealth platform across Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Germany, the United Kingdom, and the United States, providing virtual vet appointments, healthy pet checkups, follow-up care, and triage guidance on whether a case needs an in-clinic referral. The company partners with pet insurers and employers to offer covered or subsidized access to its subscription-based virtual care. FirstVet is a portfolio company of Creandum. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; FirstVet publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Imagen
providers.description: Imagen (Imagen Technologies) is an AI-enabled, sub-specialized diagnostic imaging partner for independent practices, hospitals, and health systems. It combines in-clinic imaging equipment, FDA-cleared AI algorithms, and a 24/7 teleradiology network of fellowship-trained, board-certified specialists to deliver rapid, accurate radiology interpretations, plus advanced analytics for care-gap identification. Imagen operates across 23 states, serving roughly 3.5 million patients, and is backed by GV and Threshold Ventures. The company publishes a security program covering SOC 2 Type II, the HITRUST CSF, and HIPAA. Imagen Technologies exposes no public developer API surface at this time. (Note the distinct namesake company Imagen AI, imagen-ai.com, an AI photo-editing product that does publish an API and SDK.)

providers.name: Latent
providers.description: Latent (Latent Health) is an enterprise pharmacy intelligence platform for health systems, built around a clinical agentic engine that reads the chart, reasons over payer policy and drug labels, and acts inside the electronic health record. The platform spans four modules — Identify (care-gap identification, eligibility screening, site-of-care routing), Access (prior authorization, clinical review, appeals generation, benefit routing, payer outreach), Capture (340B eligibility auditing, leakage analytics, financial dashboards), and Engage (patient outreach, queue management, outcomes analytics). Latent is chart-native and EHR agnostic, integrating with Epic, Cerner and others, and is used by more than 45 health systems including Ochsner Health, MetroHealth, Yale New Haven Health, St. Luke's Health System and Henry Ford Health, serving over two million patients annually. Founded by Sriram Somasundaram and Rishabh Jain, the company has raised $80M from Spark Capital, Transformation Capital, McKesson Ventures, Conviction, General Catalyst and Y Combinator. Latent publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; its integration surface is delivered through EHR-native deployment with health-system customers, and its security posture is published on a Vanta-hosted trust center with HIPAA-compliant data handling.

providers.name: Plume Health
providers.description: Plume Health (Plume) is a telehealth company delivering gender-affirming care to transgender and gender non-conforming people across the United States. Through a mobile app and licensed clinicians, Plume provides gender-affirming hormone therapy (estrogen and testosterone), mental health support, medical letters for surgery and identification changes, and everyday clinical care, all on a monthly membership subscription. Founded in 2019 and backed by General Catalyst, Plume operates as a HIPAA-covered, LegitScript-certified consumer healthcare provider. It is a consumer-facing care service and does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: QUIBIM
providers.description: QUIBIM is a healthcare AI company that unlocks medical imaging data to improve patient outcomes through quantitative imaging biomarkers and radiomics. Its cloud-based, tissue-agnostic platform ingests, harmonizes, and analyzes imaging data (MRI, CT, PET) to extract automated radiomics and deep-learning imaging biomarkers that support clinical decision-making and biopharma drug development. Regulated clinical products include QP-Prostate, QP-Brain, QP-Liver, QP-Breast, QP-Lung, and the QP-Insights multi-omics platform, several of which are CE and UKCA marked and integrate with hospital PACS systems. QUIBIM is ISO 27001:2022 certified and HIPAA and GDPR compliant. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; QUIBIM publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Labcorp
providers.description: Labcorp helps patients, providers, organizations, and biopharma companies guide vital healthcare decisions every day. Labcorp supports HL7 / FHIR-based integration for laboratory orders and results exchange with electronic health record (EHR) systems, but does not publish a fully open public developer portal; access is granted through health-system and biopharma integration agreements.

providers.name: Sonar Mental Health
providers.description: Sonar Mental Health provides 24/7 text-based wellbeing coaching and care navigation for youth. Trained Wellbeing Coaches lead the conversations, supported by AI tooling that surfaces context and flags risk without making independent decisions, delivering between-visit and after-hours support, escalation and care coordination to higher levels of care, and real-time insights dashboards for measurement-based care across schools, health systems, primary care, and EAP pathways. The company reports serving 20,000+ young people with higher engagement between visits, and is backed by 500 Global. There is no public developer API surface; this profile captures the company's identity, security posture (SOC 2, HIPAA), and public web properties.

providers.name: BoaConsulta
providers.description: BoaConsulta is a Brazilian digital-health platform, founded in 2012 and part of the Pixeon healthtech group, that connects patients, health professionals, and institutions. It pairs a free B2C marketplace for booking in-person consultations, teleconsultations, exams, and vaccinations with a full B2B/SaaS practice-management system (150+ integrated modules covering smart scheduling, electronic health records, telemedicine, financial management, TISS insurance billing, inventory, and automated reminders). The platform reports more than 58,000 health professionals, 1.7 million registered patients, and over 2 million appointments, with LGPD-compliant end-to-end encryption and daily automated backups. It has no public developer API; this profile is enriched from BoaConsulta's own public surfaces (llms.txt, status page, help center, blog, and legal pages).

providers.name: Dialogue
providers.description: Dialogue is a leading Canadian virtual healthcare and employee wellness provider operating an Integrated Health Platform that delivers primary care, mental health support, Employee Assistance Programs (EAP), and wellness programming to members through a single mobile and web application available 24/7/365. The company serves more than 52,000 Canadian organizations — including Sun Life, National Bank of Canada, Via Rail, Lightspeed, and Samsung — connecting employees and their families with multidisciplinary care teams of nurses, physicians, and mental health specialists. Dialogue is a consumer-facing digital health application; it does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Harris Ambulatory Care Enterprise
providers.description: Harris Ambulatory Care Enterprise (part of Harris Healthcare, a Harris Computer company) provides ambulatory healthcare software solutions including the Pulse electronic health record system. The platform supports a §170.315(g)(10) ONC certified FHIR API for third-party application developers to access patient data, provider information, and clinical resources. Pulse is deployed on-premises, so each provider hosts a separate API instance with its own base URL. Third-party developers must obtain an ONC 2015 Edition Certified API License and register with each provider organization.

providers.name: Metricwire
providers.description: Metricwire is a real-world data collection platform for ecological momentary assessment (EMA), experience sampling (ESM), and digital-health research. It helps organizations measure real-world experiences to inform treatments, service offerings, and policies. Researchers design studies, schedule time- and event-based prompts, collect participant self-reports alongside passive sensor and wearable data through native iOS and Android apps, and export the results for analysis. The platform is used across clinical trials, behavioral and public-health research, and patient-reported outcome programs, with an emphasis on data privacy and security (ISO 27001, GDPR). A production JSON API is served from api.metricwire.com and a participant/researcher application from app.metricwire.com, though Metricwire does not currently publish an open developer portal or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Accurx
providers.description: Accurx is a United Kingdom clinical communication and workflow company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in London, whose software is used across NHS primary care, secondary care, and community and mental health services to message patients, run patient triage, batch-message cohorts, book and remind appointments, and (via its Scribe product) draft clinical notes with AI. Accurx integrates around the NHS as an assured IM1 live supplier, using NHS Digital's interoperability standards for primary care and connecting bi-directionally to the GP clinical-system duopoly (EMIS Health, TPP SystmOne) and Vision, plus NHS national services including the Personal Demographics Service (PDS), NHS Single Sign-On, NHS Login, and the NHS App. Accurx is a consumer and integrator of NHS FHIR and IM1 interfaces rather than a publisher of its own public developer API: as of this review it operates no public developer portal, no self-serve REST/FHIR API, and no downloadable OpenAPI or FHIR CapabilityStatement. Third-party and trust integrations are arranged through its partnerships and integration teams under partner agreement.

providers.name: Docura Health
providers.description: Docura Health builds purpose-built software for physicians who prepare medical-legal reports — independent medical examinations (IME), qualified medical examiner (QME), agreed medical examiner (AME), permanent-and-stationary, and supplemental evaluations. The platform organizes complete case files (medical records, audio, and video), generates intelligent chronological summaries that link back to source documents, guides AMA Guides-compliant impairment ratings (5th and 6th Edition), and produces structured reports from customizable templates matched to each evaluator's practice style. Docura is HIPAA compliant with enterprise-grade end-to-end encryption and audit trails, and is backed by Y Combinator. This profile was seeded from a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from Docura Health's public website and trust center; no public developer API or documentation was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Life360
providers.description: Life360 is a family safety platform built around a location-sharing mobile app for iOS and Android, offering real-time member location, Place Alerts, location history, driving safety scores and trip history, crash detection, SOS alerts and emergency dispatch, plus digital safety features such as identity theft protection and dark web monitoring. Its hardware line, following the acquisitions of Tile and Jiobit, spans Tile Mate, Pro, Slim and Sticker Bluetooth item trackers and a cellular GPS pet tracker, sold direct and through Amazon, Best Buy, Target and Walmart. The service is sold as Free, Silver, Gold and Platinum membership tiers. Life360 publishes no public developer API, no OpenAPI, no SDKs and no developer portal — its only machine-readable surface is an agent-facing one (llms.txt, an ai-plugin manifest whose advertised OpenAPI does not resolve, and Content-Signal directives in robots.txt). This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Mon Ami
providers.description: Mon Ami is a modern data management platform built for aging and disability services providers. It unifies case management, billing and claims, information and assistance (resource directory and intake), enhanced assessments, Older Americans Act reporting (OAAPS), long-term care ombudsman workflows, a provider portal, and Medicaid administrative claiming in one connected system. Mon Ami serves state units on aging, area agencies on aging, intellectual and developmental disabilities programs, Medicaid HCBS providers, and ombudsman programs, helping them reduce administrative burden while improving outcome documentation and compliance reporting. The platform references HL7/FHIR interoperability with EHRs, managed care organizations, and state systems. Mon Ami is a Felicis portfolio company; it does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Wheel
providers.description: Wheel is a telehealth and virtual care enablement platform (Wheel Horizon) that lets digital health companies, pharmaceutical and life-sciences firms, health plans, retail pharmacies, and AI health companies launch, scale, and manage virtual care services. Wheel provides a 50-state network of board-certified clinicians, 70+ evidence-based care protocols, real-time care intelligence, and clinical operations infrastructure powering roughly 7 million virtual visits annually. Its enterprise and partner integration surface is delivered through a gated developer portal (developers.wheel.com) rather than a public self-serve API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners; the "Wheel 3" name is a portfolio-scrape artifact for Wheel (wheel.com), which also appears in the network as the `wheel` stub (backed by CRV).

providers.name: 8fit
providers.description: 8fit is a consumer health and fitness application offering personalized home workout programs (HIIT, boxing, Pilates, yoga, and meditation), custom healthy meal and nutrition plans, and holistic wellness guidance built around sustainable habit-building rather than quick fixes. Founded in Berlin and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Creandum, 8fit reached more than 40 million downloads before being acquired by Withings (a Gilde Healthcare portfolio company) in February 2022. Withings announced the discontinuation of the standalone 8fit app effective June 26, 2026, folding its nutrition and activity content into the Withings app and Withings+ service. 8fit is a mobile/web consumer app and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: Cala Health
providers.description: Cala Health is a bioelectronic medicine company that develops wearable neuromodulation therapies for chronic disease. Its FDA-cleared Cala kIQ and Cala TRIO systems deliver TAPS (Transcutaneous Afferent Patterned Stimulation) therapy through a wrist-worn device that is physician-prescribed and clinically proven to reduce action hand tremors associated with essential tremor and Parkinson's disease. Patients manage therapy and view results through the MyCala portal, and clinicians access data through the Cala 360 provider portal. Cala Health is a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company operating in the life-sciences / medical-device sector. This profile currently exposes no public developer API; enrichment has captured the company's public security, privacy, and support surface.

providers.name: PathAI
providers.description: PathAI is a Boston-based digital pathology company that builds AI-powered technology to improve the accuracy and efficiency of cancer and disease diagnosis. Its flagship AISight Image Management System is a cloud-native, open enterprise platform that laboratories and research centers use to power digital pathology workflows and run AI applications against whole-slide images. PathAI also develops proprietary machine-learning algorithms for biomarker analysis and biopharma research, backed by a network of 450+ pathologists who have contributed tens of millions of image annotations. For developers, PathAI publishes AISight Link, an open API framework that lets third-party algorithm developers integrate their solutions into the AISight workflow (AI Impressions, Fields of Interest, quantitative result reporting, and case-level tools). AISight Link is a partner-integration API without a public self-serve developer portal; access is arranged through PathAI (digitaldx@pathai.com).

providers.name: 10x Genomics
providers.description: 10x Genomics is a life sciences technology company building instruments, reagents, and software that resolve biology at single-cell and spatial resolution. Its Chromium platform delivers single-cell gene expression, immune profiling, and multiomic analysis; its Visium and Xenium platforms deliver spatial transcriptomics and in situ single-cell spatial biology. The company supports researchers with analysis software (Cell Ranger, Space Ranger, Xenium Onboard Analysis, Loupe Browser), a cloud analysis platform, and open datasets. 10x Genomics does not publish a general-purpose public REST developer API; its developer surface is command-line analysis pipelines, file-format tooling, and open-source repositories on GitHub.

providers.name: Apricot
providers.description: Apricot is an AI-native clinical documentation platform for home health and post-acute care agencies, founded by home-health operator Trent Smith and headquartered in Oklahoma. Its software cuts start-of-care (SOC) and OASIS documentation time by up to 85% and QA time by up to 40%, automating medication reconciliation, wound documentation, ICD coding recommendations, and narrative generation while capturing vitals, photos, signatures, and voice notes in the home and syncing to each agency's EMR configuration. Apricot is HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant and raised a Series A led by Insight Partners in 2025. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public web presence; Apricot currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: DayDream Dental
providers.description: DayDream Dental is a full-service dental billing and revenue cycle management (RCM) provider that runs the insurance and billing operations for dental practices and DSOs so clinical teams can focus on patient care. Services span insurance verification with custom coding breakdowns saved directly to the practice management system (PMS), clean claims submission with attachments and narratives, payment posting with accurate insurance adjustments, diligent claim follow-up every seven days until paid with denials appealed, and patient billing via text, email, and mail. DayDream operates a HIPAA-focused trust center and a client dashboard app, and publishes a blog, CDT-code and payer references, videos, and demo scheduling for onboarding new offices. This is a service company rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Genome Medical
providers.description: Genome Medical is a telehealth-enabled genetic services provider offering expert genetic counseling, test selection and ordering support, results interpretation, and clinical trial matching for individuals with rare and hereditary conditions. It partners with health systems, life sciences organizations, and genetic testing labs to scale genetic care, reduce diagnostic backlogs, and accelerate diagnoses through a proprietary clinical platform and patient portal. Genome Medical does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Headway
providers.description: Headway operates a national mental-health care platform that connects patients, therapists and psychiatrists, and insurance companies. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in New York, Headway builds the first asset-free national network of behavioral-health providers who accept insurance, handling insurance credentialing, claims management, payments, and scheduling for clinicians while letting patients search for in-network providers, book appointments online, and see costs up front. The company partners with 45+ major insurers (Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, Oxford, UnitedHealthcare, Oscar) and, as of 2026, powers 600,000+ appointments per month across all 50 states. Headway is backed by a16z, Thrive, Accel, GV, Spark Capital, and Forerunner. It maintains SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance. Headway does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Limbic
providers.description: Limbic is a clinical AI company for mental healthcare, founded in 2020 and headquartered in New York with a London engineering base. Its two products — Limbic Access, a Class IIa (UKCA) medical device for conversational patient intake, assessment and clinical decision support, and Limbic Care, an AI companion delivering guided CBT and on-demand support between therapy sessions — are embedded by health plans, health systems, behavioral health providers and NHS Talking Therapies services. Both are built on the proprietary "Limbic Layer", a clinical reasoning layer that sits between the user and a large language model to enforce validated clinical guidance. Limbic Access embeds into a provider website with a small script snippet rather than a public developer API; the company publishes no developer portal, OpenAPI definitions or SDKs, and integrates with EHR and patient management systems through customer engagements. Research code accompanying its peer-reviewed studies (including work published in Nature Medicine) is open on GitHub.

providers.name: Lucis
providers.description: Lucis is a Paris-based, AI-powered preventative health platform (Y Combinator P25; backed by General Catalyst) that helps members understand their biology through comprehensive lab testing and personalised coaching. Members receive two annual lab assessments (blood, urine, and saliva) at 450+ partner labs across Europe, producing 110+ data points across 11 body systems — metabolic, cardiovascular, hormonal, nervous, and more — which an AI engine turns into personalised action plans spanning nutrition, supplementation, sleep, activity, and mental health. The platform ingests wearable data (Garmin, Withings, Oura, Strava; Apple Watch and Whoop coming soon) for ongoing monitoring. Lucis is a consumer health product; as of this profile it exposes a member web/mobile application and a compliance portal but publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: TransCrypts
providers.description: TransCrypts is a blockchain-based identity and credential verification platform that lets individuals own, encrypt, and share verified records — employment and income history, background checks, and (with HIPAA certification) health and education credentials — directly with employers, background checkers, and other verifiers. Encrypted data is stored off-chain while cryptographic hashes are anchored on-chain, so users can prove authenticity without exposing personal data. The company reports 5M+ verifications across 4M+ users and 450+ enterprise clients, and connects to HR and payroll systems such as ADP, BambooHR, and Namely. It raised a $15M seed round led by Pantera Capital, with Techstars, Lightspeed Faction, Alpha Edison, Motley Fool Ventures, Mark Cuban, and Protocol Labs participating.

providers.name: TytoCare
providers.description: TytoCare is an AI-powered remote physical examination and virtual care company. Its FDA-cleared handheld examination device and Home Smart Clinic / Pro Smart Clinic platforms let clinicians remotely examine heart, lungs, ears, throat, skin, and temperature, serving 240+ healthcare organizations and 1.6M+ patients. TytoCare publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs — EHR and telehealth integrations are delivered through private partner channels. An Insight Partners portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Eden Health
providers.description: Eden Health was a primary and virtual care company that delivered app-based medical care, behavioral health, and care navigation to employers and their employees, integrating with health systems and insurers (backed by Insight Partners). It was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its public marketing site is no longer reachable over TLS, but its primary backend service — the "Grdn" (Guardian) API at api.edenhealth.com — still serves a Swagger 2.0 description covering patients, appointments, membership, documents, care teams, and clinician tooling.

providers.name: Almanac Health
providers.description: Almanac Health is a clinical AI company building a unified, evidence-grounded platform that delivers specialist-grade medical knowledge to clinicians at the point of care. Founded by physician-researcher Cyril Zakka, MD, whose Stanford work produced one of the first retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems for clinical medicine, the platform consolidates the medical AI ecosystem into a single interface where healthcare workers reach a library of medical AI tools through an integrated LLM assistant. It is designed to run inside existing electronic health record (EHR) systems, operate under institutional governance and controls, and stay grounded in peer-reviewed evidence rather than unverified data or pharmaceutical advertising. Almanac Health raised a $10M seed round in April 2026 led by F-Prime with participation from General Catalyst (which led the pre-seed) and Lightspeed Venture Partners. The product is currently undergoing clinical validation in academic medical centers. This profile was surfaced from General Catalyst's portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Almanac Health does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Oscar
providers.description: Oscar Health (NYSE: OSCR) is a technology-driven health insurance company founded in 2012 and headquartered in New York City. It offers individual and family health plans, small-business and ICHRA employer benefits, and Medicare Advantage in a growing set of U.S. states, pairing coverage with a consumer mobile app, 24/7 virtual urgent care, telemedicine, primary care, and concierge Care Teams. Oscar's +Oscar division licenses its full-stack technology platform (Campaign Builder and other tools) to other payers and providers. The company is NCQA-accredited across Health Plan, Utilization Management, Credentialing, Provider Network, and Health Equity programs. Oscar is a General Catalyst portfolio company. As a CMS-regulated payer it is subject to the Interoperability and Patient Access rule, though it does not currently publish an open, self-serve developer API portal.

providers.name: Novoic
providers.description: Novoic is a London-based clinical AI company building speech biomarkers for the early detection of Alzheimer's disease and cognitive impairment. Its technology analyzes how people speak - acoustic and linguistic patterns - to screen for subtle cognitive change in about ten minutes on any smart device. Products include Storyteller (automated, browser-based speech-based cognitive testing), Dashboard (an enterprise platform for running screening programs across sites with AI-assisted triage and analytics), and a Speech API for direct access to their speech processing, automated speech recognition, quality control, and speech-biomarker models. Novoic is deployed across 50+ medical institutions, partners with the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, and emphasizes HIPAA/GDPR compliance. It also publishes two open-source feature-extraction libraries, surfboard (audio) and blabla (linguistics).

providers.name: Platformable
providers.description: Platformable provides API governance, open ecosystem intelligence, and consultancy services. Their training resources, dashboards, and tools help organizations build comprehensive, automated, high quality API governance systems and participate in open digital ecosystems including open banking, digital health, and traceability.

providers.name: RealWear
providers.description: RealWear builds rugged, hands-free head-mounted and assisted-reality wearable computers (the Navigator series and HMT-1) for frontline and industrial workers in energy, manufacturing, field service, and utilities. Its Android-based devices are operated entirely by voice through the on-device WearHF service, which turns any Android app's touch controls into voice commands and can be tuned with WearML voice directives placed in UI metadata — so there is no separate SDK to install. RealWear now also ships Ari, a voice-first AI assistant (Ari OS and the Ari Cloud dashboard) with Microsoft connectors (Teams, Outlook email and calendar, contacts, Copilot), skills, and cross-session memory. Developers extend the platform with native Android, Unity, React Native, Cordova, Xamarin, and HTML apps plus custom Ari skills. This profile was surfaced as a Foundry Group portfolio company and enriched from RealWear's public developer surface.

providers.name: Rupa Health
providers.description: Rupa Health (now a Fullscript company) is a healthcare platform that lets functional and root-cause medicine practitioners order, track, and receive results from specialty and functional lab tests across hundreds of lab companies through a single unified dashboard. It provides a lab test catalog, patient result portals, practitioner ordering and billing, phlebotomy coordination, and educational resources (Rupa University, the Root Cause Medicine podcast, and a lab reference guide). Rupa integrates with a range of EHR/EMR systems used by independent practitioners but does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at this time. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Centene
providers.description: Centene Corporation is a leading managed care organization providing government-sponsored healthcare programs including Medicaid, Medicare, and Health Insurance Marketplace plans. Centene operates a developer portal at partners.centene.com publishing FHIR-based interoperability APIs under the 21st Century Cures Act and CMS Interoperability and Patient Access Rule, including Patient Access, Provider Directory, and Provider RTR (Payer Data Exchange) APIs.

providers.name: Laboratory Corporation of America (Labcorp)
providers.description: Laboratory Corporation of America Holdings, doing business as Labcorp, is a leading global life sciences company providing diagnostic, drug development, and technology-enabled solutions to improve health and lives. This repository is an alias of the labcorp index and tracks the same FHIR / HL7 integration surface.

providers.name: Aquant
providers.description: Aquant is an agentic AI platform purpose-built for servicing complex equipment, used by manufacturers and service organizations across industrial equipment, medical devices, food equipment, high-tech and electronics, printing, and energy. The platform lets teams deploy specialized service AI agents through Agent Studio and a prebuilt Agent Library, and adds Voice AI (Roger) and Vision AI so field technicians, call-center agents, customer self-service, and service leaders get expert-level guidance across the full service lifecycle from diagnosis to resolution. Aquant integrates with existing CRM and field-service systems and continuously learns from an organization's institutional service knowledge to drive service revenue, scale service teams, accelerate onboarding, and increase remote resolution rates. Aquant is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners.
