Its consumer products include Rex Nutribot, a WhatsApp AI nutrition coach; the Drop, a wearable AI camera pendant that detects meals and automatically logs calories, protein, carbs, and fats via computer vision; an AI body scanner; and personalized coaching with daily health reports. Rex also offers a white-label B2B nutrition-and-fitness AI that fitness chains and app builders integrate to add meal logging (photo, barcode, or text), recipe and meal-plan generation, workout logging, 3D body scans, and nutrition analytics under their own brand.

providers.name: Rula
providers.description: Rula is a telehealth mental health platform that connects patients with licensed therapists and psychiatric providers who accept their insurance. Operating as an in-network behavioral health marketplace across all 50 states, Rula matches individuals with more than 23,000 licensed clinicians for individual, couples, family, child, and teen therapy as well as psychiatric medication management, covering 90+ conditions including anxiety, depression, ADHD, PTSD, OCD, and addiction. Rula is in-network with 120+ insurance plans nationwide (Aetna, Cigna, Optum, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross, Kaiser), with patients paying an average of about $15 per session with insurance. Rula publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or partner API surface as of this profile; care is delivered through its patient and provider web applications.

providers.name: Science
providers.description: Science Corporation is a clinical-stage medical technology company founded in 2021 by Max Hodak and headquartered in Alameda, California, with offices in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina and Paris, France. Science develops brain-computer interface (BCI) and neural-engineering technologies to restore vision, cognition, and mobility, including the PRIMA retinal implant for patients with macular degeneration, the Biohybrid neural interface, and the Vessel perfusion platform. Through its Foundry division Science also offers MEMS production and neural-engineering services to external partners. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Science publishes no public web API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Simpatico Project
providers.description: Simpatico Project (유쾌한프로젝트, Yukwaehan Project Co., Ltd.) is a Korean B2B mental-wellness startup, backed by 500 Global, whose product Clify (클라이피, "Climb & Clarify") is an AI-based integrated mental-care and Employee Assistance Program (EAP) solution for individuals and companies. Clify uses a patented multimodal algorithm to fuse Face & Voice biosignals — blood-flow changes, micro-expressions and voice characteristics — into a roughly one-minute mental-state diagnosis (stress, anxiety, depression, burnout) that it claims exceeds 90% accuracy, and rolls the results up into an organization insight dashboard for HR (company-wide mental trends, high/low-risk teams, usage). Personal mental data is processed on-device and de-identified so it is never shared with the employer, and the company states it holds ISO 27001. Product surfaces include FAV (the Face & Voice AI diagnosis engine), an EAP counseling center, and the Clify organization-insight analytics. The public presence (clify.co.kr, an imweb-built marketing and account site) exposes no developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or webhook surface at this time.

providers.name: SteadyMD
providers.description: SteadyMD is a telehealth infrastructure and clinical-workforce company (a DocGo company) backed by Lux Capital. It supplies board-certified physicians and nurse practitioners, clinical operations, and 50-state licensing and credentialing, plus technology and telehealth APIs that let healthcare and digital-health partners launch branded, fully managed virtual care. Its APIs cover patient data submission, synchronous and asynchronous consult requests, two-way patient-clinician messaging, intake forms, clinician availability, real-time status updates, document attachments, scheduling, and reporting/SLA retrieval, offered as either a Limited (partner-EMR) or Complete (SteadyMD-EMR) integration. API documentation is provided under a business agreement via a request form; there is no public developer portal or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Talkspace
providers.description: Talkspace is a New York City-based online behavioral healthcare company founded in 2012 by Oren Frank and Roni Frank that delivers virtual therapy, psychiatry, and medication management through video, voice, messaging, and live chat. The platform connects users with licensed therapists and psychiatric providers across all 50 U.S. states, covering more than 150 mental health conditions including anxiety, depression, ADHD, bipolar disorder, OCD, PTSD, insomnia, postpartum depression, and substance use. Service lines include individual therapy for adults, teen therapy (ages 13-17), couples therapy, psychiatry with prescription management, and specialized programs for LGBTQIA+, military/veteran, and senior populations, plus the women's mental health program Chapters. Talkspace is in-network with major payers such as Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, Optum, Blue Cross Blue Shield, TRICARE, and Medicare, and sells B2B solutions (Talkspace for Business) to employers, payers, benefit consultants, educational institutions, and government agencies. The company markets Precision Therapy, an internal machine-learning and NLP system used to match members to providers and surface clinical signal. Talkspace went public on NASDAQ under ticker TALK on June 23, 2021 via a SPAC merger with Hudson Executive Investment Corp, and was acquired by Universal Health Services on March 9, 2026. Talkspace does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source repository; integrations with payers, EAPs, and benefits platforms are delivered through private partnership channels, and the platform is HIPAA, HITECH, and GDPR compliant.

providers.name: Telepatia AI
providers.description: Telepatia is an AI-native clinical platform built for Latin American healthcare. It listens to doctor-patient consultations and generates clinical documentation in real time (AI Writer), surfaces evidence-based clinical recommendations during the visit (AI Advisor), integrates with 50+ electronic health record and hospital systems such as Epic, TASY, iClinic and MV (AI Integrator), and produces analytics on protocol adherence and clinical performance (AI Business Intelligence). Founded by Nicolas Abad and backed by a16z with a $33M Series A, the platform has deployed across 25+ hospital systems in Brazil, Colombia and Mexico. As of this enrichment pass Telepatia exposes a product and web application but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Quest Diagnostics
providers.description: Quest Diagnostics is a Fortune 500 company and the world's leading provider of diagnostic information services that patients and doctors can rely on to make better healthcare decisions. Quest operates 2,000+ patient service centers, performs 200+ million tests annually, and supplies its Quanum family of solutions for connecting laboratories, EHR systems, and health plans.

providers.name: Augmedix
providers.description: Augmedix is a San Francisco-based health technology company providing ambient AI medical documentation (AI scribe) services that capture patient-clinician conversations and generate clinical notes so that physicians can focus on patient care instead of EHR data entry. Founded in 2012, the company went public on Nasdaq in 2021 (AUGX) and was acquired by Commure in October 2024, becoming part of Commure's clinician-workflow platform alongside HCA Healthcare-aligned tooling. Augmedix's product line spans three service tiers — Augmedix Go (self-service AI scribe), Augmedix Assist (AI drafting with human editing, coding, and referral-letter support, notes ready within an hour), and Augmedix Live (full-service dedicated medical documentation specialist before, during, and after the visit) — plus specialty variants for Emergency Medicine, oncology, and other specialties. The platform integrates with major EHRs including Epic, Oracle Cerner, athenahealth, Meditech, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, and iKnowMed, and is HIPAA-compliant and HITRUST-certified. Augmedix's GitHub presence consists of internal QA, scribe-app base, and ambient API automation repositories; there is no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification — integration with Augmedix is handled through enterprise EHR partnerships and the Commure clinician platform rather than a self-service developer surface.

providers.name: Bariendo Inc.
providers.description: Bariendo Inc. (now operating as Everself) is a science-forward digital health company pioneering non-surgical, endoscopic weight-loss care. Founded in 2023 by Harvard Medical School physicians Dr. Christopher C. Thompson (the inventor of Endoscopic Sleeve Gastroplasty) and Dr. Pichamol Jirapinyo, the company delivers minimally invasive procedures — ESG Stomach Tightening, gastric balloon, and revision of prior bariatric surgery — alongside weight-loss medication and a 12-month concierge care program. Its consumer platform streamlines access to these interventions across a dozen-plus U.S. locations, with financing, telehealth consultations, and ongoing weight tracking. Bariendo/Everself is a consumer and clinical health service; it publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Invitae
providers.description: Invitae (now Labcorp Invitae, following Labcorp's 2024 acquisition of select Invitae assets) is a United States medical genetics and healthcare-technology company that provides clinical-grade hereditary and somatic genetic testing across oncology, women's health, cardiology, neurology, pediatrics, and rare disease. It offers providers an online ordering portal, licensed genetic counseling, and the Gia digital assistant, and returns results into clinician workflows. Invitae's integration posture is enterprise and partner-gated rather than a self-serve public developer API: genetic test orders and results reach the electronic health record through Epic-certified interfaces and Epic Aura (Orders and Results Anywhere Network) and traditional HL7 order/result feeds delivered by a dedicated EHR integration team. As of this review no public developer portal, FHIR CapabilityStatement, SMART-on-FHIR configuration, or downloadable OpenAPI is published; programmatic access is arranged through a partnership/integration engagement in its United States home market.

providers.name: Cytovale
providers.description: Cytovale is a San Francisco-based medical diagnostics company that develops early-detection technology for sepsis. Its flagship product, IntelliSep, is the first and only FDA-cleared in vitro diagnostic test for sepsis: it uses microfluidics, high-speed video, and computer-vision algorithms to measure the biophysical rigidity of tens of thousands of white blood cells, detecting the immune activation that signals sepsis risk and returning a risk stratification in roughly eight minutes. The test runs on the Cytovale System medical device in emergency-department settings. Cytovale is venture-backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Sands Capital, and the Global Health Investment Corporation. The company operates as a clinical/diagnostics device maker and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: PocketHealth
providers.description: PocketHealth is a patient-centric medical imaging platform that lets patients access, view, store, and share their diagnostic imaging (DICOM) and reports online, and lets healthcare providers exchange imaging across institutions and networks. PocketHealth also publishes an open, RESTful developer API aimed at RIS/PACS/VNA vendors, letting them embed PocketHealth's patient enrollment, electronic consent, and background record-delivery workflows natively into their own clinical software. The developer API is partner-gated - it is free forever for RIS/PACS vendors, healthcare providers, and physicians, but the full technical reference (base URL, endpoint paths, authentication) is not published on the open web; engaged vendors are assigned a dedicated integration rep who provides testing resources and detailed documentation. As a result the APIs below are modeled from PocketHealth's public developer-program descriptions rather than a public API reference or OpenAPI definition.

providers.name: tab32
providers.description: tab32 is a cloud-based dental practice management, imaging, and analytics platform for dental practices and dental service organizations (DSOs). tab32 offers a real, commercial API - powered by Google Apigee and HIPAA / SOC 2 Type II compliant - that exposes tab32's patient, provider, schedule, charts, notes, ledger, and payments data objects to DSOs and third-party developers. Access is partner-gated, not open self-service - developers reach the API through tab32's developer API portal after establishing a partnership or enterprise relationship, and full endpoint reference, authentication, and base URL details live behind that portal rather than on the public website. The API entries below are modeled from tab32's publicly documented data objects and API messaging; their endpoint paths are not published publicly and are therefore illustrative, not confirmed.

providers.name: Viz.ai
providers.description: Viz.ai is a healthcare AI company that builds an intelligent care coordination platform. Its FDA-cleared, AI-powered software analyzes medical imaging (CT, CTA, MRI, echocardiography) to detect suspected disease — stroke (large vessel occlusion, ICH), aneurysm, pulmonary embolism, and cardiovascular conditions — and automatically alerts and connects the multidisciplinary care team in real time to accelerate diagnosis and treatment. Backed by CRV, GV, Insight Partners, Scale Venture Partners, Seedcamp, Susa Ventures, and Threshold Ventures. Viz.ai exposes no public developer API; integration is delivered through clinical/enterprise deployment, and its governance-relevant public surface is a Drata-hosted Trust Center documenting a broad security and compliance program (SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and an extensive ISO family including ISO 42001 for AI management).

providers.name: 01health
providers.description: 01Health is a UK-based health technology company building clinical infrastructure that lets specialist healthcare be delivered safely inside community and dental clinics rather than only in hospitals. Founded in 2022 by Dr Sonia Szamocki, its platform centralizes patient acquisition, clinical protocols, remote specialist oversight, treatment workflows, procurement, and financial management into a single system, currently spanning orthodontics (32Co) and sleep medicine (Aerox). 01Health is backed by Balderton Capital, Gresham House Ventures, Eka Ventures, and Wavemaker360. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal has been published to date; this profile captures the company identity and the security posture of its public web surface.

providers.name: All In
providers.description: All In Food makes organic, gluten-free nut & seed snack bars on a social-impact model — every bar purchased helps fund local nutritious-food-access initiatives such as food banks, community gardens, and meal programs across the U.S. The company is backed by Obvious Ventures (a reported $4M raise) and sells through Sprouts and Starbucks as well as its own online store. While All In is a consumer-packaged-goods brand rather than a developer platform, its Shopify storefront exposes a genuine agent-native commerce surface: a canonical agents.md document, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, a live hosted MCP endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp for agent-driven catalog search, cart, checkout and fulfillment, and Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect for buyer identity. Checkout always requires explicit human buyer approval on payment.

providers.name: Briya
providers.description: Briya builds AIRE (AI Research Environment), a privacy-first AI platform for healthcare and clinical research that lets researchers analyze real-world medical data without writing code. AIRE trains AI models on real-world data and provides domain-specific agents for literature review, hypothesis testing, population and cohort analysis, study design, and manuscript-ready output with built-in validation. Data is accessed across multiple sources without centralizing it into a warehouse, with a compliance posture aimed at HIPAA, GDPR, and FDA/EMA regulatory standards. Briya serves emerging biotech, life sciences organizations, academic institutions, and healthcare systems, with offices in New York, Nashville, and Tel Aviv. The company is backed by Insight Partners. This API Evangelist profile is an enrichment pass on a portfolio lead; Briya publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Chamber Cardio
providers.description: Chamber Cardio is a Washington, D.C.-based healthcare technology company building a cardiology-focused platform for value-based care. Chamber partners with cardiology practices and health plans to align clinical signals, workflows, and patient data so cardiologists can identify high-risk patients earlier, close gaps against treatment guidelines, and reduce administrative burden. Its workflow-integrated AI surfaces clearer signal from the large volumes of cardiovascular data generated in care, supporting better patient outcomes and financial predictability for payers as cardiology moves beyond fee-for-service. The company supports more than 500 cardiologists across seven states and raised a $60M Series A led by Frist Cressey Ventures, with participation from General Catalyst, AlleyCorp, American Family Ventures, Company Ventures, Optum Ventures, Healthworx Ventures, and Black Opal Ventures. Chamber does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal; its platform is built on a FHIR-based data stack (Medplum) with internal REST and GraphQL services.

providers.name: Galileo
providers.description: Galileo (galileo.io, formerly reached at galileohealth.com) is a value-based, digitally enabled healthcare delivery company founded by Tom X. Lee (previously Epocrates and One Medical). It delivers 24/7 primary and multi-specialty care through a mobile app, in-home visits, mobile clinics, and virtual care, combining a proprietary clinical technology platform, a recruited network of primary-care and specialist clinicians, and hospitality-style member support. Galileo operates a fully bilingual (English/Spanish) platform and serves individuals and families, employers, small businesses, and health plans through membership and population- health partnerships. It is a care-delivery business, not an API platform: as of this profile Galileo publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: MedAll
providers.description: MedAll is a UK-founded healthcare education platform on a mission to make medical education radically accessible. It hosts live and on-demand courses, conferences, workshops, webinars and training sessions for healthcare professionals, students and organisations, and provides event management tooling for registrations, feedback forms, certificates, abstracts, schedules and digital poster halls, alongside CME (continuing medical education), question banks and mobile apps for iOS and Android. The platform is used by clinicians and institutions worldwide. As of this enrichment pass MedAll publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or webhooks; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture. Backed by Seedcamp.

providers.name: Nines
providers.description: Nines was a teleradiology and medical-imaging AI startup founded in 2017 and backed by Accel and 8VC (a $16.5M Series A in 2019), co-founded by CEO David Stavens. It built FDA-cleared AI algorithms — NinesAI Emergent Triage (for intracranial hemorrhage and mass effect) and NinesMeasure (a lung-nodule algorithm) — alongside a live teleradiology practice. On 2022-02-18, Sirona Medical acquired Nines' AI technology, clinical data pipeline, machine-learning engines, and key personnel, folding the FDA-cleared devices into RadOS, Sirona's cloud-native Radiology Operating System (reporter, viewer, PACS, worklist, and platform AI). The nines.com domain now redirects to sironamedical.com. There is no public developer API today; a RadOS "Amplify" SDK (TypeScript/Python, REST + streaming APIs, event subscriptions) is on Sirona's roadmap as an early-access program for design partners.

providers.name: Pivotal Health
providers.description: Pivotal Health (formerly Radix Health) is a healthcare technology company and self-described "IDR Authority" that helps medical providers secure fair out-of-network reimbursement through the federal Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process created by the No Surprises Act. Its platform combines automated eligibility screening, dispute submission software integrated with major revenue cycle management (RCM) systems, payer data, and white-glove managed services across emergency medicine, anesthesiology, radiology, surgery, pathology, air ambulance, and hospitals and health systems. Pivotal Health is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: River Health
providers.description: River Health is an employer-sponsored virtual-first health plan operated by Mountain (joinmountain.com) that gives employees comprehensive primary and behavioral care at no cost to them. Members get unlimited virtual primary care and in-person doctor visits, behavioral health and therapy, thousands of free medications with home delivery or pharmacy pickup, free preventive care and screenings, after-hours urgent care, no-cost specialty and chronic- condition care, and free lab testing through Quest Diagnostics. Employers from small businesses to the Fortune 500 sponsor the plan; members enroll and manage care through the River Health member app at app.helloriver.com. River Health is a portfolio company of Techstars. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal has been published.

providers.name: Rovi Health
providers.description: Rovi Health is a clinical navigation platform for employer health plans that puts "a clinician in every member's pocket." Members get text-based access to registered nurse care advisors who help them find high-quality, in-network doctors and specialists, navigate their insurance benefits and coverage, and coordinate care across every stage of treatment. The company also uses AI agents to search millions of pricing and quality data points to surface the best in-network providers for complex care and to handle appointment scheduling, aiming to help employers cut 10-20% of healthcare spend while improving employee outcomes. Rovi Health was a Y Combinator (Fall 2025) company operating in the digital health, health insurance navigation, and consumer health services space. As of this enrichment pass Rovi Health publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Ruma Care
providers.description: Ruma Care is a healthcare software company that streamlines the prior authorization process for biologic and infusion medications in infusion clinics. Its AI-powered platform pulls patient and insurance data from electronic health records (EHRs) to identify payer requirements, auto-populates payer-specific prior authorization forms with clinical data, flags missing documentation, and then manages insurer communication and follow-up until an authorization is approved. Built by former infusion clinic staff, Ruma Care consolidates the manual portal, fax, and paper workflows behind buy-and-bill and infusion services into a single platform to reduce denials and accelerate patient access to biologics. Ruma Care is a Y Combinator-backed company. As of this profile the company exposes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Simplifeye
providers.description: Simplifeye is a dental practice management platform that helps practices grow and streamline front-office operations through integrated payments, online scheduling, live webchat, and patient-engagement campaigns. Its HIPAA-compliant payments product supports in-office transactions, invoicing, and customizable payment plans; its 24/7 real-time online scheduler lets patients self-book appointments; and its live webchat is staffed by real people who answer patient questions and qualify leads outside business hours. Simplifeye was acquired by Vyne Dental and integrates with the Vyne Trellis billing platform for claims, eligibility, and revenue acceleration. Simplifeye operates a private, authenticated backend (api.simplifeye.co) that powers its dashboard and patient-facing widgets, but publishes no public developer program, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: XP Health
providers.description: XP Health is an AI-powered vision benefits platform that modernizes employer vision programs with full-replacement and dual-option plans designed to reduce employee out-of-pocket eyewear costs. The platform serves more than 6,300 organizations, offering in-app prescription renewals, virtual try-on across 5,000+ eyewear styles, and a provider network reaching 90% of the U.S. population, with members saving an average of 69% on eyewear claims. Backed by QED Investors. XP Health does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: Biobeat
providers.description: Biobeat Technologies is an Israeli med-tech company whose remote patient monitoring (RPM) health-AI platform pairs a disposable short-term chest-monitor and a reusable long-term wrist-monitor - both using a photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor - to continuously track up to 13 vital signs, including FDA-cleared cuffless blood pressure, pulse rate, respiratory rate, blood oxygen saturation, temperature, stroke volume, cardiac output, and one-lead ECG (chest-monitor). Readings stream to Biobeat's HIPAA- and GDPR-compliant, cloud-based patient management platform, where clinicians view real-time data, trends, and configurable alerts. Biobeat offers programmatic data access and EMR/EHR integration as a paid add-on for hospitals, health systems, and research partners; there is no publicly documented self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Calm
providers.description: Calm is a leading consumer mindfulness, meditation, and sleep app available on iOS, Android, and web, with the consumer Calm app and the B2B Calm Health offering (formerly Calm Business, now consolidated at health.calm.com). Calm Health serves health plans, employers, and consultants with psychologist-developed clinical programs, validated mental health screenings (PHQ/GAD), personalized action plans, and the full Calm mindfulness library. Partner integration capabilities (eligibility files, SSO, SCIM, EHR/benefit-platform connectors) are sold through Calm Health enterprise contracts and are not documented in a public developer portal. There is no public REST API, no OpenAPI specification, and no self-serve developer onboarding.

providers.name: Headspace
providers.description: Headspace is a global mental health platform offering consumer mindfulness, meditation, and sleep content alongside Headspace Care (formerly Ginger) — on-demand coaching, therapy, and psychiatry — and Headspace EAP. The B2B business (Headspace for Organizations) serves 4,000+ employers, health plans, and consultants in 190+ countries with a stratified care model (AI companion Ebb, coaches, therapists, psychiatrists). Integration surfaces for enterprise customers — eligibility file feeds, SSO, SCIM, benefit-platform connectors — are delivered under enterprise contracts and are not exposed via a public developer portal. There is no public REST API, no published OpenAPI specification, and no self-serve partner onboarding.

providers.name: Modern Animal
providers.description: Modern Animal is a membership-based veterinary healthcare company operating physical primary and urgent care clinics across major U.S. metropolitan regions, combining in-clinic visits with 24/7 virtual veterinary consultations, pharmacy and prescription management, dental care, surgery, and preventive care. It runs a subscription membership model (All Access, Essential, and Pay As You Go tiers) with transparent, upfront pricing and a companion mobile app for booking and virtual care. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and susa-ventures. Modern Animal is a consumer veterinary brand and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Oshi Health
providers.description: Oshi Health is a virtual, whole-person gastrointestinal (GI) care clinic delivering insurance-covered telehealth to patients with digestive conditions such as IBS, GERD, Crohn's disease, and ulcerative colitis. Care is provided by a coordinated team of GI providers, registered dietitians, and gut-brain behavioral health specialists, and is offered to members through major health plans and employers. Oshi Health is a patient-facing healthcare services company rather than an API producer; it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched with the artifacts the company genuinely publishes.

providers.name: Proximie
providers.description: Proximie is a health-tech company building a cloud platform it describes as the operating system for intelligent operating rooms, connecting surgical teams, medical devices, and data for remote telementoring, telesurgery, session recording, and AI-powered surgical insights across 500+ facilities in 50 countries. For developers, Proximie ships a pre-release C++ SDK (media streaming and session management, with an internal REST layer) and runs a Development Partners program that lets OEMs and medtech companies embed real-time connectivity, secure data routing, and white-label collaboration into their own devices. Proximie also open-sources WebRTC/Janus tooling (jarust, janus-mobile-sdk). Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund.

providers.name: Sully AI
providers.description: Sully AI is a US-based healthcare AI company that ships a portfolio of "AI employees" for clinical and administrative work — including an AI Scribe that turns patient conversations into structured, HIPAA-compliant notes, an AI Receptionist for scheduling and front desk, an AI Triage Nurse for patient engagement, an AI Medical Coder for autonomous ICD-10 coding, an AI Pharmacist, and an AI Consultant for chart prep. The platform integrates with Epic, Cerner, MEDITECH, Athenahealth, Allscripts, Veradigm, and 50+ other EHRs. Beyond the end-user products, Sully exposes a public REST API covering audio transcription (file upload and real-time WebSocket streaming), clinical note generation (SOAP and custom templates), medical coding extraction (ICD-10, CPT, SNOMED), note templates, and a medical consensus alpha feature, with asynchronous results delivered over webhooks. Official Apache-2.0 licensed TypeScript/Node and Python SDKs are published under the sullyai GitHub org, and an Odiggo-maintained sully-api-demo repo showcases end-to-end usage. Sully's revenue model is SaaS subscriptions to healthcare providers, hospitals, and digital health platforms.

providers.name: Medtronic
providers.description: Medtronic is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Medtronic API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: TheraNest
providers.description: TheraNest (now marketed as Ensora Mental Health) is a behavioral and mental health practice management and EHR platform for therapists, counselors, psychologists, and social workers. It covers client intake, scheduling, telehealth, clinical documentation and notes, treatment plans, client portals, insurance billing and claims, and reporting. TheraNest is the flagship mental health product of Ensora Health (formerly Therapy Brands). As of this review, Ensora does not publish a documented, self-serve public developer API for TheraNest - integration is via partnerships, HIPAA-gated interoperability, and contact-sales arrangements rather than an open developer portal. The API entries below are logical resource groupings modeled from the product surface; their endpoints are NOT documented public endpoints (endpointsModeled true).

providers.name: Thyrocare
providers.description: Thyrocare Technologies Limited is an Indian chain of diagnostic and preventive-care laboratories headquartered in Navi Mumbai, founded in 1996. Built around a centralized, highly automated laboratory model, it focuses on affordable preventive health checkups, thyroid and pathology testing, and sells through a nationwide network of DSA (Direct Selling Agent) franchise partners. Norwest Venture Partners invested pre-IPO, and PharmEasy (API Holdings) acquired a majority stake in 2021. Its partner order-booking API (TechSo/BTS) is gated behind the DSA program and publishes no public OpenAPI.

providers.name: Solv Health
providers.description: Solv Health operates a consumer marketplace (solvhealth.com and the Solv app) for booking same-day urgent care, primary care, and lab appointments, plus a provider-facing platform (scheduling, intake, patient acquisition, reputation management, messaging, payments) sold to clinics and health systems. There is no self-serve public developer API or published API reference on solvhealth.com; API access is gated behind a sales-led partnership. Solv states it exposes "interoperable APIs" that power custom booking experiences on partner websites and apps, a "Final Mile" API/network that lets digital-first and virtual-care partners (e.g. Included Health) hand patients off to real-time same-day appointment availability at Solv's national network of urgent care clinics, and bidirectional EHR interoperability (APIs, HL7, FHIR, and RPA) that syncs patient demographics, appointment status, and documents with systems like Epic, Athena, Cerner, Allscripts, DrChrono, eClinicalWorks, Experity, and NextGen. None of these capabilities have a published base URL, endpoint reference, or self-serve API key signup; access is provisioned per partner/clinic inside a commercial contract.

providers.name: Prenetics
providers.description: Prenetics Global Limited (NASDAQ: PRE) is a consumer healthcare and longevity company whose flagship brand is IM8, a science-backed daily-nutrition and longevity supplement line co-founded with David Beckham that reached roughly $120M in annual recurring revenue within its first year. The company's IM8 Health direct-to-consumer storefront runs on Shopify and exposes an agent-native commerce surface: it publishes an /llms.txt agent guide and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp that advertises a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) shopping endpoint, letting AI agents search the catalog, build carts, and drive buyer-approved checkout via Shop Pay, Google Pay, and Shopify card handlers. Prenetics itself publishes no separate developer/API program; the agent-commerce surface is the IM8 Health UCP/MCP storefront.

providers.name: AZmed
providers.description: AZmed is a Paris-based medical-imaging AI company whose Rayvolve AI Suite assists radiologists by automatically analyzing X-rays and other studies. Its applications include AZtrauma (fracture detection), AZchest (chest imaging), AZmeasure (anatomical measurements), AZboneage (bone-age assessment) and AZnod (CT nodule detection). The software integrates into existing radiology workflows rather than being exposed as a public developer API, and is deployed across 2,500+ healthcare centers in 55+ countries, analyzing over 15 million X-rays annually, backed by 10+ peer-reviewed publications. As of this profile AZmed does not publish a public REST API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Eleanor Health
providers.description: Eleanor Health is a value-based, whole-person addiction and mental health care provider delivering virtual and in-person treatment for substance use disorders — including opioid, alcohol, stimulant, and prescription drug use — through medication for addiction treatment (MAT), therapy, peer recovery support, and health coaching. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, the company partners with health plans and Medicaid programs across multiple U.S. states to deliver measurement-based, outcomes-driven behavioral healthcare. Eleanor Health is backed by General Catalyst. It does not publish a public developer API program; member scheduling and clinical records run on athenahealth, and its public GitHub organization holds internal engineering tooling rather than a first-party API.

providers.name: Grail
providers.description: GRAIL, Inc. is a healthcare company headquartered in Menlo Park, California, focused on detecting cancer early, when it can be cured. Its flagship product, the Galleri multi-cancer early detection (MCED) test, uses a single blood draw and methylation-based genomic sequencing to screen for a signal shared across more than 50 types of cancer, many of which lack any recommended screening today. GRAIL runs large clinical programs including the PATHFINDER, PATHFINDER 2, and NHS-Galleri studies, and distributes Galleri through health plans, employers, and partners such as Quest Diagnostics and Junction. GRAIL is a portfolio company of investors including GV and SV Angel. It does not publish a first-party public developer API; programmatic access to Galleri ordering is offered through third-party diagnostic infrastructure partners.

providers.name: Healthera
providers.description: Healthera is a United Kingdom digital-health and patient-engagement company, founded in 2015 by Cambridge University students and headquartered in Cambridge, England. It runs a patient-facing pharmacy app and website for ordering NHS prescriptions and medicines online and booking pharmacy services (Pharmacy First, treatments, vaccinations), alongside a pharmacy-facing SaaS "Patient Experience Platform" used by 1,700+ community pharmacies to manage repeat prescriptions, bookings, marketing, and delivery. In November 2022 Healthera became the first pharmacy app to integrate with the NHS Electronic Prescription Service (EPS), and it connects to NHS Digital / NHS England systems plus third-party platforms such as myGP, eConsult, Cegedim Rx Pharmacy Manager, Medpoint, Royal Mail, and Uber for same-hour delivery. Healthera markets custom integration APIs to pharmacy and brand partners, but as of this review it publishes no public developer portal, no self-serve API documentation, and no machine-readable contract; its api.healthera.co.uk "Healthera Core" host is a private backend and exposes no FHIR CapabilityStatement. Integration is partner-gated rather than self-serve.

providers.name: Junomedical
providers.description: Junomedical (now Qunomedical) is a Berlin-based digital health company founded in 2015 by Dr. Sophie Chung that connects patients with professionally-vetted doctors and clinics for high-quality medical treatments at home and abroad. The consumer platform (qunomedical.com) offers free assessments, price matching, 24/7 patient support, and personalized treatment matching across specialties including plastic surgery, hair transplants, dentistry, oncology, orthopedics, reproductive medicine, and weight-loss surgery, serving roughly 10,000 patients a month. The company also builds Qunosuite, a patient-relationship-management (PRM) SaaS for healthcare providers. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company operates a consumer marketplace and a provider SaaS but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Lifesum
providers.description: Lifesum is a Stockholm-based digital health company whose consumer mobile application helps people improve their well-being through food logging, calorie and macronutrient tracking, personalized meal plans, recipes, and habit building. Backed by Balderton Capital, the company operates a subscription business-to-consumer product across iOS and Android in a dozen languages. As of this profile Lifesum publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or partner API portal, so this entry is an identity-only company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API profile.

providers.name: Waymark
providers.description: Waymark is a healthcare technology and services company that scales value-based, community-based care for people enrolled in Medicaid. In partnership with health plans and primary care providers, Waymark trains and employs local care teams — community health workers, care coordinators, licensed therapists, and pharmacists — and equips them with predictive technology that identifies high-risk patients and coordinates interventions addressing the social determinants of health such as housing, food security, transportation, medication management, and behavioral health. The model is designed to reduce avoidable hospitalizations and emergency room visits, and Waymark operates community-based care across Ohio, Virginia, and Washington. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), NEA, Lux Capital, and CVS Health Ventures. Waymark publishes no public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures the company identity and its public web presence.

providers.name: Delve Bio
providers.description: Delve Bio is a genomic diagnostics company commercializing clinical metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for infectious disease diagnosis. Its flagship test, Delve Detect, analyzes all nucleic acids in a single cerebrospinal fluid sample to simultaneously detect bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites, screening against a curated database of more than 68,000 pathogen species to diagnose meningitis and encephalitis with results in roughly 48 hours. The company is the exclusive licensee of the University of California San Francisco (UCSF) mNGS technology developed at the Center for Next-Gen Precision Diagnostics, founded by Charles Chiu, Joe DeRisi, Michael Wilson, Pardis Sabeti, and Matthew Meyerson, and backed by investors including GV. Delve Bio operates as a CAP/CLIA-certified clinical laboratory serving labs and clinicians; it exposes no public developer API surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a gv portfolio lead.

providers.name: Luminai
providers.description: Luminai is an AI-powered automation platform for health system operations, marketed as "The AI Platform for Health System Operations." It automates complex, high-volume healthcare back-office workflows including referral intake and processing, provider inbox automation, patient registration, orders and referrals, pharmacy renewals, payor contract management, denial appeals, and underpayment recovery. The company reports over 12 million automations driven, an average 5.3x ROI, and a 48-day average time to value, with enterprise-grade security and flexible deployment options (on-premises, VPC, or fully managed). Luminai is SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR compliant. It is a venture-backed company in the General Catalyst portfolio. Luminai does not publish a public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its public identity and security posture.

providers.name: Mend
providers.description: Mend is a HIPAA-compliant telehealth and patient engagement platform for mental and behavioral healthcare organizations, powering appointment scheduling, automated reminders, secure video visits, digital intake forms and consents, patient messaging, payments, and AI no-show prediction. Mend integrates with EHR and practice-management systems through a combination of HL7, SFTP, and an API served from api.mendfamily.com. That API exists and is used by Mend's own portal for session initialization and signaling, but its reference documentation is delivered through a login-gated customer knowledge base rather than a public developer portal, so Mend's programmatic surface is best characterized as partner- and customer-gated rather than openly self-serve.

providers.name: Rad AI
providers.description: Rad AI is a San Francisco based healthcare technology company that builds generative and machine-learning software for radiology. Its products help radiologists work faster and reduce burnout: Rad AI Reporting is a generative AI reporting platform, Rad AI Impressions automatically generates customized report impressions (reported to save radiologists 60+ minutes per shift), and Rad AI Continuity manages follow-up of incidental findings. The company is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA certified and is backed by Khosla Ventures. Rad AI markets its clinical products directly to health systems and imaging groups and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and compliance program for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Abbott Laboratories
providers.description: Abbott Laboratories is a global healthcare company that develops, manufactures, and markets pharmaceuticals, medical devices, diagnostics, and nutritional products. Abbott's digital health portfolio includes the FreeStyle Libre continuous glucose monitoring system, cardiac monitoring devices, and connected diagnostics platforms that enable data sharing between patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers.

providers.name: Roche
providers.description: F. Hoffmann-La Roche is a Swiss multinational healthcare company with two divisions: Roche Pharma and Roche Diagnostics. Roche does not publish a general public developer API but exposes interoperability through the navify diagnostics platform, the cobas infinity laboratory software, and an open-source GitHub presence focused on data-science tooling such as pyreadstat, foxops, and OligoGym.

providers.name: Bodyport
providers.description: Bodyport is a San Francisco healthcare technology company delivering remote heart-failure monitoring. Its FDA-cleared Cardiac Scale captures hemodynamic biomarkers through a patient's feet in under 30 seconds and transmits the readings over cellular to care teams within minutes. The company's Congestion Index algorithm combines multiple hemodynamic biomarkers to detect worsening heart failure earlier than standard weight-based rules, and its connected Care Platform surfaces monitoring, alerts, and care coordination through a clinical dashboard and a patient portal. Bodyport works with health systems and pharma partners including Geisinger, Boehringer Ingelheim, Stanford, Brigham and Women's Hospital, Duke, and Yale. The company publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its product, portal, and compliance surfaces.

providers.name: Generation Lab
providers.description: Generation Lab is a longevity science company founded in 2023 by Alina Su, UC Berkeley bioengineer Dr. Irina Conboy, and Michael Suswal, and backed by an $11M seed round led by Accel (Accel's first longevity bet). Its flagship SystemAge test measures biological age across roughly 460 biomarkers spanning 19 to 21 physiological systems and organs from an at-home, needle-free blood collection, returning a personalized aging report and science-backed action plan that ranges from lifestyle and supplement guidance to clinical interventions. The test is distributed through 300+ clinic partners across 18 countries and via a patient/provider portal. Generation Lab publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its public web, product, and legal surfaces.

providers.name: MedThread
providers.description: MedThread is an AI-powered Health Information Management (HIM) platform built specifically for long-term and post-acute care facilities — skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), nursing homes, assisted living facilities (ALFs), and rehabilitation centers. The platform digitizes paper records with AI-powered scanning, runs continuous automated audits for documentation completeness and regulatory compliance, monitors CMS quality metrics (rehospitalization, pressure ulcers, antipsychotic use), and provides a compliance dashboard, provider portal, and patient-facing Personal Health Record (PHR). MedThread advertises FHIR compatibility and pre-built EHR integrations (Epic, Cerner, Allscripts, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, Meditech, athenahealth, Greenway, Practice Fusion) via a secure API. Techstars-backed and based in Miami, FL. No public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification is published at this time.

providers.name: Elephant Healthcare
providers.description: Elephant Healthcare is a global health-technology company, headquartered in the UK, that partners with governments to digitise and strengthen public health systems across Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Its flagship product, ElephantOS, is a mobile- and offline-first electronic health record (EHR) that streamlines clinical workflows for primary and secondary care facilities, serving over 19 million contracted patients across Nigeria, Kenya and Pakistan. The company also builds Elephant Nudge, a clinical co-pilot that guides and rewards quality of care, and Elephant Platform, an emerging AI-driven marketplace that connects clinicians to third-party healthcare software, medical devices and supply-chain partners. Elephant is backed by General Catalyst and Seedcamp. As of July 2026 the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Forus (fka Tandem Health)
providers.description: Forus (formerly Tandem Health) is a US healthcare technology company building an AI-powered network that connects doctors, pharmacies, payers, and biopharma to bring new therapies to patients. Its platform automates the medication-access workflow end to end: prior authorization submissions, appeal-letter generation, insurance enrollment forms, benefit verification, pharmacy routing, patient status communication, PA renewal tracking, and affordability-program enrollment. It integrates with major EHRs so prescribers can submit directly, covers any drug/plan/pharmacy across all 50 states, and is HIPAA-compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified. The company publishes an engineering blog at build.forus.com but does not currently expose a public developer API. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures.

providers.name: K Health
providers.description: K Health is a clinical AI and virtual primary care company founded in 2016 and headquartered in New York City. Its platform pairs an AI-led symptom investigation and intake engine with a 24/7 team of credentialed clinicians to deliver primary care, urgent care, mental health, and medical weight management. K Health licenses its clinical AI to health systems — including Cedars-Sinai, Mayo Clinic, Hackensack Meridian Health, Hartford HealthCare, Mass General Brigham, and Northwell Health — where it triages patients, combines intake with EMR data (Epic/MyChart), and automates clinical documentation. The company has raised more than $380M and was valued at roughly $900M as of 2024. K Health is a B2B2C consumer health application with no public developer API; integrations are handled through partners such as Health Gorilla for lab ordering. This profile was surfaced as a ggv-capital portfolio lead and enriched with verified public identity, link, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: LEAP
providers.description: LEAP is cloud-based legal practice management software for law firms, covering matter and contact management, document automation and court forms, time recording, billing, and trust accounting, tightly integrated with Microsoft 365. LEAP operates a LEAP Developer Console and LEAP Marketplace (developer.leap.build / console.leap.build) through which approved third-party developers build REST-based integrations (an "API Reference" is versioned there, e.g. v1.0.4, v1.0.5), but the technical reference - endpoint paths, base URL, and authentication schema - sits behind developer registration and an app review process rather than a public, self-serve API reference. There is no publicly published OpenAPI document, public base URL, or anonymous API key signup. Existing Marketplace integrations (Xero, Zoom, InfoTrack, LawTap, and others) confirm the API surface is real and in production use, but its concrete shape is not publicly disclosed.

providers.name: PictorLabs.ai
providers.description: Pictor Labs develops AI-powered virtual staining technology for histopathology and digital pathology laboratories. Its platform generates diagnostic-quality tissue stains computationally in minutes rather than the hours or days required by traditional chemical staining, preserving precious tissue samples for additional downstream testing. Products include ClearStain for direct virtual H&E sequencing and DeepStain and ReStain for flexible, repeatable multi-stain tissue analysis. The technology integrates with existing whole-slide scanner platforms (partners include Hamamatsu and Proscia) and offers cloud or on-premise deployment. Virtual stains are currently labeled For Research Use Only. Pictor Labs is a venture-backed company in the Insight Partners portfolio. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: SmarterDx
providers.description: SmarterDx builds clinical AI software that hospitals and health systems use to analyze the complete record of every patient and fully capture the value of care delivered. Its products span the revenue cycle — SmarterPrebill, SmarterCharges, SmarterDenials, SmarterNotes, and SmarterUtilization — surfacing missing diagnoses, validating charges, defending against payer denials, improving clinical documentation, and supporting utilization management decisions. The company serves 85+ health systems and operates as an enterprise B2B vendor: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or self-serve sign-up, and maintains HIPAA compliance to protect the privacy of its health-system partners.

providers.name: Phare Health
providers.description: Phare Health builds AI tools for healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM), focused on medical coding and clinical documentation improvement (CDI). Its platform analyzes complete electronic health records to generate accurate, compliant medical codes and to catch coding errors before bills are submitted. Products include Phare Audit (a pre-bill safety net that screens encounters for errors), Phare Autonomous (automated coding of simpler cases with explainability), and Phare Analytics (coding workflow and financial monitoring). The UK-founded, General Catalyst-backed company has been acquired by R1 and integrated into its R37 lab division. Phare Health operates as a closed B2B product and publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or status page at this time.

providers.name: Amera
providers.description: Amera (Amera Health Solutions) is a Seattle-based, Y Combinator (Fall 2025) healthcare technology company that automates claims processing workflows for health insurance payers, third-party administrators (TPAs), and self-insured employers. Its normalization engine ingests messy claim inputs from any source — EDI, PDFs, paper, fax, and proprietary/non-standard formats — and turns them into adjudication-ready, structured data that plugs into existing claims cores via API, EDI, or SFTP. The platform automates validation, reconciliation, stop-loss reporting, and real-time visibility and analytics, reducing plan administration costs and cutting carrier submission times from weeks to minutes while keeping full audit trails and HIPAA compliance. Founded in 2025 by Louise Tanski and Deep Kapur (both formerly of Rupa Health), Amera already works with payers and plan administrators representing roughly 100,000 members. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; Amera does not yet publish a public developer portal or API specification.

providers.name: Ansible Health
providers.description: AnsibleHealth is a virtual-first, doctor-led telemedicine practice specializing in the management of COPD, congestive heart failure, and other chronic pulmonary and cardiac conditions from home. Serving patients across 50+ states, it combines virtual diagnosis and personalized treatment plans, remote patient monitoring of vitals like heart rate and blood oxygen, virtual physical therapy, smoking-cessation coaching, and medication and durable-medical-equipment ordering to reduce hospitalizations and emergency-room use. The practice accepts Medicare, Medicaid, and most major commercial insurance plans. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a patient-facing website but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: asieris
providers.description: Asieris Pharmaceuticals is a China-based biopharmaceutical company developing innovative therapies in genitourinary tumors and women's health. Its focus areas span urologic oncology (bladder cancer diagnosis and treatment), women's health, and breast and gynecologic oncology, with marquee assets Vesique (APL-1202) for bladder cancer and Cevira (APL-1702), a non-invasive photodynamic therapy for cervical precancerous lesions. The company runs three proprietary R&D platforms (TIMN, TAIDD, DDC). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; as a biopharma company it publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: At-Home-Doc
providers.description: At-Home-Doc (now branded MetaDoc) is a Qatar-based healthcare SuperApp operated by Medihealth Solutions (MOPH Licence No. 2066) offering round-the-clock virtual and in-person medical care. Patients book on-demand video consultations, in-network clinic appointments, or home doctor visits through the app, alongside pharmacy delivery, lab-at-home services, family insurance packages, and a Med Coins loyalty rewards program. The platform bundles Meta Doc (virtual clinics for practitioners), Meta Patient (a patient community), and Medi Shop into a single consumer healthcare experience delivered over iOS and Android. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Aumio
providers.description: Aumio (Aumio GmbH) is a Berlin-based children's digital-health company behind a freemium sleep, meditation, and mindfulness mobile app for kids aged roughly 0-10 and their families. The app offers 200+ audio experiences - bedtime stories, soundscapes, white noise, sleep music, and guided meditations - added to weekly, with parts of the subscription reimbursed by German statutory health-insurance providers as a certified prevention course. Founded in 2020 and backed by Partech, Aumio operates as a consumer B2C product (iOS, Android, and web) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web and domain footprint.

providers.name: Breathwrk
providers.description: Breathwrk is a consumer health and performance app offering guided breathing exercises to reduce stress, improve sleep, boost energy, and enhance athletic and social performance. It packages more than 50 science-backed breathing techniques with music, haptics, coach-led classes, and progress tracking across calming, sleep, energizing, performance, and social categories. Breathwrk is available on iOS and Android with free and Pro subscription tiers plus a Breathwrk for Business program for organizations, and the company is now part of Peloton. Breathwrk publishes no public API, SDK, or developer program; this profile is maintained by API Evangelist and reflects the company's live web presence and security posture.

providers.name: Bumame
providers.description: Bumame is an Indonesian healthcare provider ("Elevating Indonesian Healthcare") delivering global-standard health screening and preventive-care services to Indonesian families. It operates a network of clinics and offers medical check-up packages, laboratory testing, vaccination and boosters, maternal and child health services, early cancer screening and genetic DNA testing, vitamin infusions, home care, doctor consultations, and corporate health programs, with online appointment booking. Backed by 500 Global. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface has been found to date.

providers.name: Carbon Health
providers.description: Carbon Health is a technology-enabled healthcare provider offering primary, urgent, virtual, and pediatric care through in-person clinics and telemedicine across the United States. It operates on its own clinical technology platform (CarbyOS) and offers services including same-day appointments, cold/flu/COVID testing, STI/STD testing, sports physicals, occupational and workplace health, and clinical research for sponsors. Carbon Health was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or FHIR patient-access surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity, public web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Clear Labs
providers.description: Clear Labs builds automated next-generation sequencing (NGS) platforms that combine laboratory robotics, cloud software, and bioinformatics to deliver genomic data and actionable insights. Its product lines span oncology research (Clear Dx), infectious-disease and microbial genomics (Clear Ix), and food-safety pathogen testing (Clear Safety) for organisms such as Listeria and Salmonella. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, Menlo Ventures, and Wing Venture Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Clear Labs publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation as of this profile; the record captures company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: CMR Surgical
providers.description: CMR Surgical is a British medical-device company headquartered in Cambridge, UK, founded in 2014 (as Cambridge Medical Robotics). It develops Versius, a small, modular and portable robot-assisted surgical system used across urology, general, gynaecological and thoracic surgery, and Versius Plus, its next-generation platform cleared by the US FDA in December 2025. More than 45,000 patients have been treated globally, making Versius one of the most widely used soft-tissue robotic surgery platforms. CMR reached unicorn status in 2019 and raised a $600M Series D at a $3B valuation in 2021, backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, GE Healthcare, ABB Technology Ventures and others. Its digital ecosystem (Versius Connect, Versius Team, Versius Clinical Insights) is a login-gated clinical surface; CMR publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs or developer portal.

providers.name: ContinuumCloud
providers.description: ContinuumCloud is a Tampa, Florida-based provider of cloud software purpose-built for behavioral health and human services organizations. Its integrated suite spans three products: Welligent, an electronic health record (EHR) platform for caseload management, scheduling, clinical documentation and revenue-cycle management; DATIS e3, a unified human capital management (HCM) and payroll system covering recruiting, onboarding, timekeeping, talent management and workforce analytics; and CaredFor, a patient-engagement platform that builds online communities connecting clients, alumni and families. Formerly known as Behavioral Holdings and founded in 2020, the company draws on 25+ years of domain focus and is backed by Battery Ventures. ContinuumCloud does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or MCP server at this time; this profile captures its company identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Curology
providers.description: Curology is a direct-to-consumer skincare and telehealth company founded in 2014 and based in San Francisco, California. It pairs online dermatology providers (dermatologists, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants) with custom-compounded prescription topical treatments for acne, anti-aging, and other skin concerns, delivered as a subscription. Care is delivered through a secure telemedicine platform where patients complete a skin assessment, upload photos, and receive a personalized formula plus ongoing provider messaging. Curology is a portfolio company of Forerunner Ventures and IVP. It operates as a consumer web and mobile product and does not publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company as part of the API Evangelist health/telehealth network.

providers.name: Daybreak
providers.description: Daybreak Health is a B2B mental health company that delivers teletherapy and mental health programs for K-12 students (ages 5-19) in partnership with school districts and health plans. Its services include one-on-one teletherapy, in-person and hybrid onsite programs, universal mental health screeners, and mental health classes, with programs tailored for BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, and low-income student populations. Daybreak is a care-delivery organization sold to schools and payers rather than a developer platform; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer or API surface. This APIs.json profile captures the company's public web properties and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Delfi Diagnostics
providers.description: DELFI Diagnostics is a precision oncology company, founded in 2019 and built on research from the Johns Hopkins Kimmel Cancer Center, that combines machine learning with genome-wide analysis of cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns (an approach it calls DNA fragmentomics, or "fragmentomes") to develop accessible, blood-based cancer screening and treatment-monitoring tests. Its first commercial product, FirstLook Lung, is a laboratory-developed liquid biopsy screening test for lung cancer that runs from a simple blood draw and reports a high negative predictive value; the company also offers DELFI-TF for treatment monitoring and partners with health systems and pharmaceutical researchers. DELFI operates a CLIA laboratory and is headquartered in Palo Alto, California. This profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network; DELFI publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Digital Diagnostics
providers.description: Digital Diagnostics is a healthcare AI company based in Coralville, Iowa, founded by Dr. Michael Abramoff. It builds autonomous artificial-intelligence diagnostic systems that make a medical diagnosis at the point of care without requiring a physician to interpret the result. Its flagship product, LumineticsCore (formerly IDx-DR), was the first FDA-cleared autonomous AI diagnostic system and detects diabetic retinopathy from fundus images in about 30 seconds, reimbursed under CPT code 92229 and integrated with EHR systems such as Epic. A companion product, SphereDx, provides securely hosted diagnostic result management. The company is a portfolio company of 8vc and is researching additional indications including glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative disease detection via retinal imaging. Digital Diagnostics emphasizes ethical, equitable AI ("AI the right way") and holds ISO 13485:2016 quality-management certification. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Eucalyptus
providers.description: Eucalyptus (eucalyptus.health) is a global digital healthcare company founded in 2019 and headquartered in Sydney, Australia, that builds and operates patient-first telehealth clinics. It runs four consumer digital-health brands — Juniper (women's weight management and menopause), Pilot (men's health, hair loss, sexual health and weight), Software (clinical-grade skincare and dermatology) and Kin (reproductive, fertility and postpartum care) — across Australia, the United Kingdom, Germany, Japan and Canada, pairing licensed practitioners with technology and connected-care tooling. Eucalyptus was acquired by Hims & Hers Health in June 2026. This profile is a consumer-facing healthtech company: it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time, so enrichment is limited to verified corporate identity, published website properties, a responsible-disclosure program, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Fabric
providers.description: Fabric is a healthcare care-enablement platform (formerly Zipnosis, rebranded to Fabric in 2024) that streamlines access to virtual and in-person care. Its AI-powered system automates patient intake, symptom gathering, triage, and routing while integrating with existing EMR systems, serving health systems, hospitals, health plans, employers, and brokers. The platform spans synchronous and asynchronous virtual care delivery, an AI navigation and symptom-checking assistant, an intelligent provider directory and scheduling layer, a 50-state virtual clinical network (Evo), and patient engagement and care-management pathways. Fabric was assembled through the acquisitions of Zipnosis, GYANT, MeMD, TeamHealth Virtual Care, and UCM Digital Health. As of this profile Fabric does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; integration is EMR-based and arranged via sales.

providers.name: Feel Therapeutics
providers.description: Feel Therapeutics, an IQVIA business, is a Digital Precision Medicine company on a mission to reinvent how mental health is diagnosed, managed and cared for by bringing objective data, continuous passive measurement and novel digital biomarkers into mental healthcare. Rather than relying on episodic, subjective self-reported questionnaires, Feel develops digital biomarkers from wearable and passive sensor data to enable continuous, objective monitoring. Its solutions span the Feel Digital Precision Medicine Platform (DPMP), Feel DTx precision digital therapeutics, drug-plus / beyond-the-pill programs, and a wearable monitoring device. The company partners with pharma and biotech to advance clinical development, real-world evidence (RWE), and commercialization strategies, and has run 20+ research studies with 3000+ participants.

providers.name: Forta (fka Montera)
providers.description: Forta Health (formerly Montera, Inc.) is a San Francisco based digital health company making Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) therapy accessible to families of children with autism spectrum disorder. Forta connects families with board-certified behavior analysts (BCBAs) and registered behavior technicians (RBTs) for evidence-based care delivered virtually across 43 states and in-home in select cities, with active parent involvement, no waitlists, and Medicaid and insurance accepted. Backed by Insight Partners, the company raised a $55M Series A. It operates a consumer-facing healthcare service and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Freenome
providers.description: Freenome is an early cancer detection company founded in 2014 that develops blood-based screening tests to catch cancer in its earliest, most treatable stages. It combines multiomics laboratory science with artificial intelligence and machine learning to read multiple biological signals from a single blood draw, an approach it calls Personalized Cancer Detection. Its SimpleScreen portfolio includes tests for colorectal and lung cancer, validated through clinical research programs such as the PREEMPT CRC study. Freenome is a clinical diagnostics and life-sciences company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead (backed by a16z, CRV, DCVC, and GV) and enriched with the public identity, legal, and domain-security signals available from its website.

providers.name: Gabit
providers.description: Gabit is a one-stop health and wellness platform on a mission to add more healthy years to people's lives. Headquartered in Gurugram, India and founded in 2022 by Gaurav Gupta (ex-Zomato cofounder) and Arpana Shahi, Gabit treats health as an interconnected system across four pillars — fitness, nutrition, sleep, and mindfulness. Its consumer ecosystem spans the titanium Gabit Smart Ring, a smart body-composition scale, at-home Blood Work diagnostics, a continuous glucose monitor (CGM), the Sweden-born Näck nutrition supplement line, all-good-no-harm skincare, and coached Fitness & Nutrition Plans — all unified in the Gabit app, which tracks 150+ biomarkers and includes the free PEP AI health coach. India is the primary market, with Ring-only storefronts in the UAE and UK and an informational US/global page.

providers.name: Halo Health
providers.description: Halo Mental Health (Halo Health) operates same-day mental health urgent care clinics, offering immediate psychiatric assessments, medication management, crisis intervention, individual and group therapy, and teletherapy for adults and children ages eight and older. Founded by Paul Manley with medical director Dr. Vahid Osman, the Joint Commission-accredited provider runs clinics in Central Las Vegas and Summerlin, accepts commercial insurance and Medicaid, and is building the largest network of urgent cares dedicated to same-day mental health services. Backed by 8vc. Halo Health publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile captures its identity, web presence, and domain security posture.

providers.name: HD
providers.description: HD is an AI-native healthcare marketplace and patient-navigation platform for emerging Southeast Asia, headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand. Its consumer surface, HDmall, is a health, dental, aesthetics, and surgery marketplace that lets patients compare transparent pricing and book online across 30,000+ services from 3,000+ clinics and hospitals in Thailand (hdmall.co.th) and Indonesia (hdmall.id). AI-powered navigation turns patient symptoms into personalized, safety-checked care recommendations, and HDcare adds human-led, AI-assisted concierge support for complex surgical cases. The platform has navigated over 500,000 patients. HD is a consumer-facing healthtech operator with no public developer API or portal; the strongest machine-readable surface it publishes today is an llms.txt guiding LLMs to its canonical content. HD is a portfolio company of Partech, added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: Healint
providers.description: Healint is a Singapore-headquartered digital health company best known for Migraine Buddy, the world's largest migraine and headache tracking and research platform, used by more than three million people to log attacks, symptoms, triggers, medications, and treatment outcomes. The company applies machine learning, mobile sensor technologies, and analytics to help people manage migraine and other neurological conditions, and to generate real-world evidence for clinicians, researchers, and pharmaceutical partners. Healint and Migraine Buddy are now part of Aptar Digital Health, whose regulated companion apps, patient-support software, and drug-delivery platforms operate across more than 120 countries on HIPAA-compliant infrastructure. Healint does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Heltia
providers.description: Heltia is a Turkish digital mental-health and employee-wellbeing platform (an Employee Assistance Platform, EAP) that connects individuals and corporate employees with licensed psychologists and dietitians for online therapy, counseling and nutrition support. Its consumer app offers video sessions with experts, self-assessment tests (anxiety, depression, OCD, motivation) and an expert-reviewed blog, while its corporate products — Esenlik (wellbeing), Sağlık Yönetimi (health management) and brokerage — give employers measurable workforce mental-health programs. Backed by Northzone. Heltia does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK or documentation surface.

providers.name: Imperative Care
providers.description: Imperative Care is a U.S. medical technology company founded in 2015 by Fred Khosravi, neurosurgeon L. Nelson Hopkins, M.D., and Amar Sawhney, Ph.D., that develops connected interventional devices to elevate care for people affected by devastating vascular diseases such as ischemic stroke, venous thromboembolism, and acute limb ischemia. Its portfolio spans the Zoom Stroke System (including Zoom intracranial access and aspiration catheters and Continuous Dual Aspiration / CDAT technology) for fast, effective clot removal, the Symphony Thrombectomy System for venous thromboembolism, and the Prodigy Thrombectomy System for acute limb ischemia, with the Telos robotic-assisted platform in development in partnership with Proximie. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of D1 Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Imperative Care publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical developer portal; this profile captures its public web, security, and corporate surface.

providers.name: Internet Brands
providers.description: Internet Brands is a KKR-owned digital media and software company, founded in 1998 and headquartered in El Segundo, California, that operates a portfolio of vertical franchises across health, dental, legal, and auto/home/travel markets. Its brands include WebMD and Medscape (health), WebMD Ignite and PulsePoint (health engagement), Henry Schein One and Dentrix (dental SaaS), FindLaw and Avvo (legal), and CarsDirect and Fodor's (auto, home, and travel). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and Redpoint Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. The holding company does not publish a single unified public developer API; developer surfaces live with its individual operating brands.

providers.name: Iodine Software (Waystar)
providers.description: Iodine Software is a healthcare AI company whose AwareCDI suite applies clinical machine learning to the mid-revenue cycle, surfacing clinical documentation integrity (CDI) gaps, prioritizing high-impact cases, and automating physician queries so hospitals and health systems capture the complete patient story for more accurate coding, quality metrics, and revenue capture. Its Concurrent, Retrospective, and Interact modules integrate directly into existing EHR and coding workflows rather than exposing a public developer API. Founded in Austin, Texas, Iodine was acquired by revenue-cycle technology company Waystar in October 2025, and its products, blog, newsroom, and legal pages now live under waystar.com and its AltitudeAI platform. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Bain Capital Ventures portfolio company in the healthcare sector.

providers.name: Journey Medidtation
